lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A DevOps engineer needs to create a Linux AMI automatically. The ID of the newly created AMI must be saved in a location from which other build pipelines can retrieve the ID programmatically.  
  
What is the **MOST** cost-effective way to accomplish this?

options.text: Build a pipeline in AWS CodePipeline to download and save the latest operating system Open Virtualization Format (OVF) image to an Amazon S3 bucket. Customize the image by using the guestfish utility. Use the virtual machine (VM) import command to convert the OVF to an AMI. Store the AMI identification output as an AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store parameter.

Create an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook with values instructing how the image should be created. Build a pipeline in AWS CodePipeline to execute the runbook to create the AMI. Store the AMI identification output as a Systems Manager Parameter Store parameter.

Build a pipeline in AWS CodePipeline to take a snapshot of an Amazon EC2 instance running the latest version of the application. Start a new EC2 instance from the snapshot and update the running instance by using an AWS Lambda function. Take a snapshot of the updated instance and convert it to an AMI. Store the AMI identification output in an Amazon DynamoDB table.

Launch an Amazon EC2 instance and install Packer. Configure a Packer build with values defining how the image should be created. Build a Jenkins pipeline to invoke the Packer build to create an AMI. Store the AMI identification output in an Amazon DynamoDB table.

questions.explanation:
AWS Systems Manager Automation includes managed runbooks and actions for creating Amazon Machine Images, and the AMI-creation action returns the new image ID. Storing that ID in Systems Manager Parameter Store makes it available programmatically to other pipelines while avoiding the additional compute, tooling, and database infrastructure required by the alternatives.

A software-as-a-service (SaaS) company uses AWS Elastic Beanstalk to deploy its primary .NET application. The Elastic Beanstalk environment is configured to use Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling and Elastic Load Balancing (ELB) for its underlying Amazon EC2 instances.  
  
The company is experiencing incidents where EC2 instances are marked unhealthy and terminated by Auto Scaling groups following a failed ELB health check. The company's DevOps team must create a solution that notifies the operations team whenever an Auto Scaling group terminates EC2 instances for any existing client environments.  
  
What should the DevOps team do to fulfill this requirement?

options.text: Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe the email addresses of all operations team members to the SNS topic. Apply a notification configuration for the autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH notification type to all the existing Auto Scaling groups.

Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Add an AWS Lambda function trigger to the SQS queue. Apply a notification configuration for the autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH notification type to all the existing Auto Scaling groups.

Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe the email addresses of all operations team members to the SNS topic. Apply a notification configuration for the autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE notification type to all the existing Auto Scaling groups.

Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Add an AWS Lambda function trigger to the SQS queue. Apply a notification configuration for the autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE notification type to all the existing Auto Scaling groups.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling can publish Amazon SNS notifications for instance lifecycle events. The `autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE` event is emitted for a successful instance termination, and email endpoints subscribed to the SNS topic receive the notification, including information about the terminated instance and the reason for termination.

**Learn more:** [Amazon SNS notification options for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-sns-notifications.html) · [PutNotificationConfiguration API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/APIReference/API_PutNotificationConfiguration.html)

A DevOps engineer has created an AWS CloudFormation template that includes the following snippet:  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783829209691-hd6psvge.png)  
  
When the template is launched, CloudFormation rolls back and reports this error message: `Received 0 SUCCESS signal(s) cut of 1.`  
  
Which combination of actions should the DevOps engineer take to resolve this error? (Choose two.)

options.text: Update the UserData attribute to use the cfn-signal helper script.
Update the AutoScalingGroup resource with a DependsOn LaunchConfig.
Update the LaunchConfig resource type to AWS::EC2::LaunchTemplate.
Increase the CreationPolicy ResourceSignal Timeout.
Remove the CreationPolicy attribute. Create new WaitHandle and WaitCondition resources.

questions.explanation:
An Auto Scaling group's `CreationPolicy` requires the specified number of success signals before CloudFormation can complete creation. The instance user data must run `cfn-signal` after its initialization work completes; otherwise CloudFormation receives no success signal. The `PT5M` timeout is the default and may be too short for installing bootstrap tools and copying the S3 data, so it should be increased to allow initialization to complete and send the signal.

**Learn more:** [cfn-signal - AWS CloudFormation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/cfn-signal.html) · [CreationPolicy attribute - AWS CloudFormation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-attribute-creationpolicy.html)

options.text: Create a scheduled Amazon CloudWatch Events rule to execute an AWS Systems Manager automation document that checks if any EC2 instances are scheduled for retirement once a week. If the instance is scheduled for retirement, the automation document will hibernate the instance.
Enable EC2 Auto Recovery on all of the instances. Create an AWS Config rule to limit the recovery to occur during a maintenance window only.

Reboot all EC2 instances during an approved maintenance window that is outside of standard business hours. Set up Amazon CloudWatch alarms to send a notification in case any instance is failing EC2 instance status checks.
Set up an AWS Health Amazon CloudWatch Events rule to execute AWS Systems Manager automation documents that stop and start the EC2 instance when a retirement scheduled event occurs.

questions.explanation:
AWS Health publishes a scheduled EC2 retirement event for affected Amazon EBS-backed instances. An EventBridge rule can match that event and invoke an AWS Systems Manager Automation document to stop and start each affected instance, which migrates it from the retiring host and automates the required response.

**Learn more:** [Running operations on EC2 instances automatically in response to AWS Health events](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/health/latest/ug/automating-instance-actions.html) · [Scheduled events for Amazon EC2 instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/monitoring-instances-status-check_sched.html)

A company’s legacy application relies on IAM user credentials to access resources in the company’s AWS Organizations organization. A DevOps engineer must ensure that new IAM users cannot be created unless the employee creating the IAM user is on an exception list.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Attach an Organizations SCP with an explicit deny for all iam:CreateAccessKey actions with a condition that excludes StringEquals for aws:username with a value of the exception list.
Attach an Organizations SCP with an explicit deny for all iam:CreateUser actions with a condition that includes StringNotLike for aws:username with a value of the exception list.

Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule with a pattern that matches the iam:CreateAccessKey action with an AWS Lambda function target. The function will check the user name and account against an exception list. If the user is not on the exception list, the function will delete the user.

Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule with a pattern that matches the iam:CreateUser action with an AWS Lambda function target. The function will check the user name and account against an exception list. If the user is not on the exception list, the function will delete the user.

questions.explanation:
An Organizations SCP can apply an explicit deny to `iam:CreateUser` when the requesting principal’s `aws:username` does not match an exception-list entry. SCPs set the maximum available permissions for affected accounts, and an explicit deny overrides otherwise granted permissions, so unlisted IAM users are prevented from creating new IAM users.

**Learn more:** [SCP syntax - AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps_syntax.html) · [Policy evaluation logic - AWS IAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_evaluation-logic.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses AWS CloudFormation to manage an application running on Amazon EC2 instances. The instances belong to an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group. The company wants its infrastructure to be immutable.  
  
A DevOps engineer must implement a solution that replaces two EC2 instances at a time whenever operating-system configuration updates are required or new Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) are needed. At least four EC2 instances must remain running while an update is in progress.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Modify the CloudFormation template to include an UpdatePolicy attribute for the Auto Scaling group. Include the AutoScalingRollingUpdate policy with MinInstancesInService of 4 and MaxBatchSize of 2. Whenever a software update is needed, alter either or both of the ImageId and UserData of the AWS::EC2::LaunchTemplate and update the stack.

Set the Auto Scaling group’s minimum capacity to 4. Create an AWS CodeDeploy deployment group that has an in-place deployment type. Select Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group for the environment configuration. Whenever a new revision is available, create a new CodeDeploy deployment that has a deployment configuration of CodeDeployDefault HalfAtATime.

Set the Auto Scaling group's minimum capacity to 4. Create an AWS CodeDeploy deployment group that has a blue/green deployment type. Select Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group for the environment configuration. Whenever a new revision is available, create a new CodeDeploy deployment that has a deployment configuration of CodeDeployDefault HalfAtATime.

Modify the CloudFormation template to include a StackPolicy. Designate an AutoScalingReplacingUpdate policy to control the update. Specify MinInstancesInService of 4 and MaxBatchSize of 2. Whenever a software update is needed, alter either or both of the ImageId and UserData of the AWS::EC2::LaunchTemplate and update the stack.

questions.explanation:
CloudFormation's `UpdatePolicy` with `AutoScalingRollingUpdate` performs a rolling replacement of an Auto Scaling group's instances. `MaxBatchSize: 2` limits concurrent replacements to two instances, while `MinInstancesInService: 4` requires at least four instances to remain in service. Changing the launch template `ImageId` or `UserData` and updating the stack applies the new immutable instance configuration through that rolling update.

**Learn more:** [UpdatePolicy attribute - AWS CloudFormation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-attribute-updatepolicy.html) · [Configure Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling resources with CloudFormation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/quickref-ec2-auto-scaling.html)

A DevOps engineer is creating a multistage AWS CodePipeline pipeline to build, verify, stage, test, and deploy an application. A manual approval stage is needed between the test and deploy stages. The development team uses a custom chat tool that supports webhooks and needs near-real-time notifications.  
  
How should the DevOps engineer configure pipeline-activity status updates and approval requests so they are posted to the chat tool?

options.text: Create an Amazon CloudWatch Logs subscription that filters on CodePipeline Pipeline Execution State Change. Publish subscription events to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe the chat webhook URL to the SNS topic, and complete the subscription validation.
Create an AWS Lambda function that is invoked by AWS CloudTrail events. When a CodePipeline Pipeline Execution State Change event is detected, send the event details to the chat webhook URL.

Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule that filters on CodePipeline Pipeline Execution State Change. Publish the events to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Create an AWS Lambda function that sends event details to the chat webhook URL. Subscribe the function to the SNS topic.

Modify the pipeline code to send the event details to the chat webhook URL at the end of each stage. Parameterize the URL so that each pipeline can send to a different URL based on the pipeline environment.

questions.explanation:
AWS CodePipeline sends pipeline execution state-change events directly to Amazon EventBridge, whose rules can route those events to Amazon SNS and AWS Lambda in near real time. A Lambda function subscribed to the SNS topic can format the event or approval payload and invoke the custom chat webhook. Manual approval actions support publishing approval-request notifications to an SNS topic through their `NotificationArn` configuration, so the same SNS-to-Lambda integration can deliver approval requests.

**Learn more:** [Monitoring CodePipeline events](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/detect-state-changes-cloudwatch-events.html) · [Add a manual approval action to a stage](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/approvals.html)

On the next CodePipeline run, the pipeline enters a **FAILED** state during the build stage. The DevOps engineer confirms that the correct Systems Manager parameter path is configured for the environment-variable values that changed. The DevOps engineer also confirms that the environment variable type is **Parameter**.  
  
Why did the pipeline fail?

options.text: The CodePipeline IAM service role does not have the required IAM permissions to use Parameter Store.
The CodePipeline IAM service role does not have the required IAM permissions to use the aws/ssm KMS key.
The CodeBuild IAM service role does not have the required IAM permissions to use Parameter Store.
The CodeBuild IAM service role does not have the required IAM permissions to use the aws/ssm KMS key.

questions.explanation:
AWS CodeBuild resolves Parameter Store environment variables by using its own service role. That role must allow the `ssm:GetParameters` action for the referenced parameter path; otherwise the build cannot retrieve the values and fails.

**Learn more:** [Build specification reference for CodeBuild](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/build-spec-ref.html) · [Troubleshooting AWS CodeBuild](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/troubleshooting.html)

A company uses AWS to deploy an application. The development team must automate its deployments. The team created an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that deploys the application to Amazon EC2 instances with AWS CodeDeploy after AWS CodeBuild builds it.  
  
The team wants to add automated testing to the pipeline to verify that the application is healthy before deploying the code to the EC2 instances. The team also requires a manual approval action before the application is deployed, even when the tests succeed. The testing and approval must be implemented at the lowest cost and with the simplest management solution.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a manual approval action after the build action of the pipeline. Use Amazon SNS to inform the team of the stage being triggered. Next, add a test action using CodeBuild to perform the required tests. At the end of the pipeline, add a deploy action to deploy the application to the next stage.

Create a test action after the CodeBuild build of the pipeline. Configure the action to use CodeBuild to perform the required tests. If these tests are successful, mark the action as successful. Add a manual approval action that uses Amazon SNS to notify the team, and add a deploy action to deploy the application to the next stage.

Create a new pipeline that uses a source action that gets the code from the same repository as the first pipeline. Add a deploy action to deploy the code to a test environment. Use a test action using AWS Lambda to test the deployment. Add a manual approval action by using Amazon SNS to notify the team, and add a deploy action to deploy the application to the next stage.

Create a test action after the build action. Use a Jenkins server on Amazon EC2 to perform the required tests and mark the action as successful if the tests pass. Create a manual approval action that uses Amazon SQS to notify the team and add a deploy action to deploy the application to the next stage.

questions.explanation:
AWS CodePipeline supports CodeBuild as a managed Test action, so tests can run immediately after the build and prevent later stages from proceeding when they fail. A subsequent Manual approval action pauses execution until an authorized user approves it; Amazon SNS can notify the team that approval is required. Placing CodeDeploy after those actions ensures deployment occurs only after successful tests and manual approval.

**Learn more:** [AWS CodeBuild build and test action reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/action-reference-CodeBuild.html) · [Add a manual approval action to a pipeline in CodePipeline](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/approvals-action-add.html)

A company stores proprietary data in Amazon S3. The development team creates buckets for new projects every day. The security team needs to make sure that every current and future bucket has encryption, logging, and versioning enabled. In addition, buckets must never allow public read or write access.  
  
What should a DevOps engineer do to satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Enable AWS CloudTrail and configure automatic remediation using AWS Lambda.
Enable AWS Config rules and configure automatic remediation using AWS Systems Manager documents.
Enable AWS Trusted Advisor and configure automatic remediation using Amazon CloudWatch Events.
Enable AWS Systems Manager and configure automatic remediation using Systems Manager documents.

questions.explanation:
AWS Config rules continuously assess S3 bucket configurations, including existing resources and new configuration changes, so they can identify buckets that lack the required encryption, logging, versioning, or public-access protections. AWS Config can associate automatic remediation actions with Systems Manager Automation documents, which apply the required corrective configuration to noncompliant buckets. AWS provides managed Config rules for detecting public S3 read and write access, and Systems Manager remediation runbooks can configure S3 Block Public Access.

**Learn more:** [Remediating Noncompliant Resources with AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/remediation.html) · [Setting Up Auto Remediation for AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/setup-autoremediation.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has granted an externally hosted third-party vendor product access to the company’s AWS account. The vendor product performs various AWS actions in the AWS account and requires various IAM permissions. The company granted this access by creating an IAM user, attaching IAM policies, and entering the IAM user credentials into the vendor product.  
  
A security review finds that the vendor’s access is excessively permissive. The company wants to apply the principle of least privilege while continuing to give the vendor permission to perform only the actions it has performed during the last 6 months.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** effort?

options.text: Use AWS Identity and Access Management Access Analyzer to generate a new IAM policy based on the IAM user’s AWS CloudTrail history. Replace the IAM user policy with the newly generated policy.

Use AWS Identity and Access Management Access Analyzer to generate a new IAM policy based on the IAM user’s AWS CloudTrail history. Attach the newly generated policy as a permissions boundary to the IAM user.

Use AWS Identity and Access Management Access Analyzer to discover the last accessed information for the IAM user and to create a new IAM policy that allows only the services and actions that the last accessed review identified. Replace the IAM user policy with the newly generated policy.

Use AWS Identity and Access Management Access Analyzer to discover the last accessed information for the IAM user and to create a new IAM policy that allows only the services and actions that the last accessed review identified. Attach the newly generated policy as a permissions boundary to the IAM user.

questions.explanation:
IAM service last accessed information reports activity for at least 400 days and can include action-level data for supported services. It can therefore be used to identify the vendor IAM user's access over the required six-month period and create a replacement identity policy that permits only the identified services and actions. CloudTrail-based policy generation is limited to a 90-day analysis period. A permissions boundary sets a maximum permission set but does not grant permissions itself.

**Learn more:** [View last accessed information for IAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies_last-accessed-view-data.html) · [IAM Access Analyzer policy generation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access-analyzer-policy-generation.html)

A company operates a single AWS account in which active development takes place. The company's security team has deployed Amazon GuardDuty, AWS Config, and AWS CloudTrail in the account. The security team needs near-real-time notifications for only high-severity GuardDuty findings. The security team uses an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic for notifications from other security tools in the account.  
  
How can a DevOps engineer satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Configure an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule that detects GuardDuty findings. Use an input transformer to detect high-severity event patterns. Configure the rule to publish a message to the SNS topic.

Configure an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule that detects noncompliance with the guardduty-non-archived-findings AWS Config managed rule for high-severity GuardDuty findings. Configure the EventBridge (CloudWatch Events) rule to publish a message to the SNS topic.

Configure an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule with an event pattern that matches GuardDuty ListFindings API calls with a high severity level. Configure the rule to publish a message to the SNS topic.

Configure an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule with an event pattern that matches GuardOuty findings that have a high severity level within the event. Configure the rule to publish a message to the SNS topic.

questions.explanation:
Amazon GuardDuty sends finding events directly to Amazon EventBridge in near real time. Input transformers modify matched event content rather than filtering events; AWS Config compliance events and CloudTrail API-call events are not the direct GuardDuty finding stream needed for this notification path.

A company wants to establish a continuous delivery pipeline. The company keeps its application code in a private GitHub repository. The company must deploy application components to Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS), Amazon EC2, and AWS Lambda. The pipeline must support manual approval actions.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS CodePipeline with Amazon ECS, Amazon EC2, and Lambda as deploy providers.
Use AWS CodePipeline with AWS CodeDeploy as the deploy provider.
Use AWS CodePipeline with AWS Elastic Beanstalk as the deploy provider.
Use AWS CodeDeploy with GitHub integration to deploy the application.

questions.explanation:
AWS CodePipeline can use a GitHub connection as a source and can pause execution for a manual approval action. Its supported action providers include Amazon ECS and Amazon EC2 deploy actions, plus an AWS Lambda action, enabling one pipeline to deploy components to each required target.

**Learn more:** [Valid action providers in CodePipeline](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/actions-valid-providers.html) · [GitHub connections for CodePipeline](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/connections-github.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has recently launched an application that is more popular than anticipated. The company wants to ensure that the application can scale for increasing demand and provide reliability by using multiple Availability Zones (AZs). The application runs on a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). A DevOps engineer created an Auto Scaling group across multiple AZs for the application. Instances launched in the newly added AZs are not receiving application traffic.  
  
What is the likely cause of this issue?

options.text: Auto Scaling groups can create new instances in a single AZ only.
The EC2 instances have not been manually associated to the ALB.
The ALB should be replaced with a Network Load Balancer (NLB).
The new AZ has not been added to the ALB.

questions.explanation:
An ALB routes traffic only to targets in Availability Zones that are enabled on the load balancer. Adding AZs to an Auto Scaling group does not automatically enable those AZs and their subnets on the ALB; targets in an unenabled AZ do not receive load-balancer traffic. When an Auto Scaling group is attached to the target group, instances it launches are registered automatically.

**Learn more:** [Application Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/application-load-balancers.html) · [What is an Application Load Balancer?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/introduction.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has built a serverless web application hosted on AWS. The application consists of Amazon S3, Amazon API Gateway, several AWS Lambda functions, and an Amazon RDS for MySQL database. The company uses AWS CodeCommit to store the source code. The source code combines AWS Serverless Application Model (AWS SAM) templates and Python code.  
  
A security audit and penetration test find that user names and passwords used to authenticate to the database are hardcoded in CodeCommit repositories. A DevOps engineer must implement a solution that automatically detects and prevents hardcoded secrets.  
  
What is the **MOST** secure solution that fulfills these requirements?

options.text: Enable Amazon CodeGuru Profiler. Decorate the handler function with @with_lambda_profiler(). Manually review the recommendation report. Write the secret to AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store as a secure string. Update the SAM templates and the Python code to pull the secret from Parameter Store.

Associate the CodeCommit repository with Amazon CodeGuru Reviewer. Manually check the code review for any recommendations. Choose the option to protect the secret. Update the SAM templates and the Python code to pull the secret from AWS Secrets Manager.

Enable Amazon CodeGuru Profiler. Decorate the handler function with @with lambda profiler(). Manually review the recommendation report. Choose the option to protect the secret. Update the SAM templates and the Python code to pull the secret from AWS Secrets Manager.

Associate the CodeCommit repository with Amazon CodeGuru Reviewer. Manually check the code review for any recommendations. Write the secret to AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store as a string. Update the SAM templates and the Python code to pull the secret from Parameter Store.

questions.explanation:
Amazon CodeGuru Reviewer supports Python repositories in AWS CodeCommit and automatically detects hardcoded passwords, database connection strings, user names, and other unprotected secrets during code review. AWS recommends moving hardcoded database credentials to Secrets Manager, where they can be securely retrieved by the application rather than stored in source code.

A company application runs on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. A DevOps engineer must ensure that at least four application servers are running at all times. Whenever an application update is required, the engineer creates a new AMI with the updated configuration and updates the AWS CloudFormation template with the new AMI ID. After the stack update completes, the engineer manually terminates the old instances one at a time, confirming that each new instance is operational before continuing. The engineer needs to automate this process.  
  
Which action will require the **LEAST** manual effort going forward?

options.text: Update the CloudFormation template to include the UpdatePolicy attribute with the AutoScalingRollingUpdate policy.
Update the CloudFormation template to include the UpdatePolicy attribute with the AutoScalingReplacingUpdate policy.
Use an Auto Scaling lifecycle hook to verify that the previous instance is operational before allowing the DevOps engineer's selected instance to terminate.
Use an Auto Scaling lifecycle hook to confirm there are at least four running instances before allowing the DevOps engineer's selected instance to terminate.

questions.explanation:
AWS CloudFormation's `AutoScalingRollingUpdate` update policy replaces Auto Scaling group instances in batches when the launch configuration or launch template changes. Configuring `MinInstancesInService` to 4 maintains at least four in-service application servers while old instances are updated, and `WaitOnResourceSignals` can make the rollout wait for new instances to report readiness before proceeding.

**Learn more:** [UpdatePolicy attribute - AWS CloudFormation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-attribute-updatepolicy.html)

A company’s application development team uses Linux-based Amazon EC2 instances as bastion hosts. Inbound SSH access to these bastion hosts is limited to specific IP addresses through their associated security groups. The company’s security team wants a notification whenever the security-group rules are changed to permit SSH access from any IP address.  
  
What should a DevOps engineer do to meet this requirement?

options.text: Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule with a source of aws.cloudtrail and the event name AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress. Define an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic as the target.

Enable Amazon GuardDuty and check the findings for security group in AWS Security Hub. Configure an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule with a custom pattern that matches GuardDuty events with an output of NON_COMPLIANT. Define an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic as the target.

Create an AWS Config rule by using the restricted-ssh managed rule to check whether security groups disallow unrestricted incoming SSH traffic. Configure automatic remediation to publish a message to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic.

Enable Amazon Inspector. Include the Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures-1.1 rules package to check the security groups that are associated with the bastion hosts. Configure Amazon Inspector to publish a message to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic.

questions.explanation:
The AWS Config managed rule `restricted-ssh` evaluates security groups as NON_COMPLIANT when inbound SSH traffic is allowed from an unrestricted CIDR such as `0.0.0.0/0` or `::/0`. It runs on configuration changes, and AWS Config automatic remediation uses Systems Manager Automation documents, allowing a custom automation action to publish the noncompliance notification to an Amazon SNS topic.

**Learn more:** [restricted-ssh - AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/restricted-ssh.html) · [Remediating Noncompliant Resources with AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/remediation.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A DevOps engineer is deploying a new version of a company’s application by using an AWS CodeDeploy deployment group associated with Amazon EC2 instances.  
  
After a period of time, the deployment fails. The engineer discovers that every event associated with the specific deployment ID has a **Skipped** status, and the code was not deployed to the instances associated with the deployment group.  
  
What are valid reasons for this failure? (Choose two.)

options.text: The networking configuration does not allow the EC2 instances to reach the internet via a NAT gateway or internet gateway, and the CodeDeploy endpoint cannot be reached.
The IAM user who triggered the application deployment does not have permission to interact with the CodeDeploy endpoint.
The target EC2 instances were not properly registered with the CodeDeploy endpoint.
An instance profile with proper permissions was not attached to the target EC2 instances.
The appspec.yml file was not included in the application revision.

questions.explanation:
For EC2/On-Premises CodeDeploy deployments in which all lifecycle events are skipped, target instances must be able to reach the CodeDeploy and Amazon S3 public endpoints over HTTPS; private-subnet instances require suitable outbound routing, such as through a NAT gateway. The CodeDeploy agent also requires an attached IAM instance profile with the necessary permissions to communicate with CodeDeploy and retrieve the application revision.

**Learn more:** [Troubleshoot EC2/On-Premises deployment issues - AWS CodeDeploy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/troubleshooting-deployments.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is testing a web application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The instances operate in an Auto Scaling group spanning multiple Availability Zones. The company uses a blue/green deployment process with immutable instances to deploy new software.  
  
During testing, users are automatically logged out of the application at random times. Testers also report that all users are logged out whenever a new version of the application is deployed. The development team needs a solution that ensures users stay logged in through scaling events and application deployments.  
  
What is the **MOST efficient** way to ensure users remain logged in?

options.text: Enable smart sessions on the load balancer and modify the application to check for an existing session.
Enable session sharing on the load balancer and modify the application to read from the session store.
Store user session information in an Amazon S3 bucket and modify the application to read session information from the bucket.
Modify the application to store user session information in an Amazon ElastiCache cluster.

questions.explanation:
Session state must be externalized from the individual EC2 instances so that any replacement or newly deployed instance can retrieve it. Amazon ElastiCache provides a shared, low-latency store for session information, allowing the application tier to remain stateless across Auto Scaling events and blue/green immutable deployments. AWS Well-Architected guidance specifically identifies Amazon ElastiCache as a destination for offloaded session state and notes that this design permits servers to be replaced without availability impact.

**Learn more:** [REL05-BP06 Make services stateless where possible — AWS Well-Architected Framework](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/2023-04-10/framework/rel_mitigate_interaction_failure_stateless.html) · [HA and automatic scaling for ASP.NET Web Forms applications on AWS — AWS Prescriptive Guidance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/migration-asp-net-web-forms/ha-scaling.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company plans to migrate a legacy application to AWS and build a deployment pipeline using only AWS services. A DevOps engineer is moving all application code from a Git repository to AWS CodeCommit while retaining the repository history. The engineer has configured all CodeCommit permissions, installed the Git client and AWS CLI on a local computer, and is ready to migrate the repository.  
  
Which actions should be taken?

options.text: Create the CodeCommit repository using the AWS CLI. Clone the Git repository directly to CodeCommit using the AWS CLI. Validate that the files were migrated, and publish the CodeCommit repository.

Create the CodeCommit repository using the AWS Management Console. Clone both the Git and CodeCommit repositories to the local computer. Copy the files from the Git repository to the CodeCommit repository on the local computer. Commit the CodeCommit repository. Validate that the files were migrated, and share the CodeCommit repository.

Create the CodeCommit repository using the AWS Management Console. Use the console to clone the Git repository into the CodeCommit repository. Validate that the files were migrated, and publish the CodeCommit repository.

Create the CodeCommit repository using the AWS Management Console or the AWS CLI. Clone the Git repository with a mirror argument to the local computer and push the repository to CodeCommit. Validate that the files were migrated, and share the CodeCommit repository.

questions.explanation:
A history-preserving migration to AWS CodeCommit uses `git clone --mirror` to create a bare local copy containing the source repository’s Git history and references, followed by a push to the destination CodeCommit repository. After the migration, the repository contents can be validated and the CodeCommit repository shared with the team. The destination repository may be created through either the AWS Management Console or the AWS CLI.

**Learn more:** [Migrate a Git repository to AWS CodeCommit](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/how-to-migrate-repository-existing.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A web application has been deployed with an AWS Elastic Beanstalk application. The application developers are concerned about high latency in two areas of the application:  
  
- HTTP client requests to a third-party API  
- MySQL client-library queries to an Amazon RDS database  
  
A DevOps engineer must collect trace data to diagnose the issues.  
  
Which steps will collect the trace information with the **LEAST** application changes and performance impact?

options.text: Add additional logging to the application code. Use the Amazon CloudWatch agent to stream the application logs into Amazon OpenSearch Service. Query the log data in OpenSearch Service.
Instrument the application to use the AWS X-Ray SDK. Post trace data to an Amazon OpenSearch Service cluster. Query the trace data for calls to the HTTP client and the MySQL client.
On the AWS Elastic Beanstalk management page for the application, enable the AWS X-Ray daemon. View the trace data in the X-Ray console.
Instrument the application using the AWS X-Ray SDK. On the AWS Elastic Beanstalk management page for the application, enable the X-Ray daemon. View the trace data in the X-Ray console.

questions.explanation:
The AWS X-Ray SDK instruments the application to generate trace segments and subsegments for outbound HTTP requests and supported database calls, including MySQL queries. The X-Ray daemon on the Elastic Beanstalk instances relays that trace data to AWS X-Ray, where it is analyzed in the X-Ray console. Elastic Beanstalk can enable the daemon directly, but the daemon needs SDK-generated trace data.

**Learn more:** [Configuring AWS X-Ray debugging](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/environment-configuration-debugging.html) · [Running the X-Ray daemon on AWS Elastic Beanstalk](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/xray/latest/devguide/xray-daemon-beanstalk.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances. A DevOps engineer must aggregate the application log files into a central system so the company's application team can search them. A critical error message appears periodically in those log files. The DevOps engineer must email the application team whenever these error messages occur.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements in the **MOST** operationally efficient manner?

options.text: Configure the unified Amazon CloudWatch agent on the EC2 instances to publish the application logs files to a CloudWatch log group. Configure a metric filter on the CloudWatch log group to detect the critical errors and to create a custom metric. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Configure a CloudWatch alarm to use the custom metric to notify the SNS topic. Subscribe the application team's email address to the SNS topic.

Install the Amazon Kinesis agent on the EC2 instances. Configure the Kinesis agent with the location of the log files. Stream the logs to a Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream with an Amazon CloudWatch metrics stream as a destination. Configure an AWS Lambda function to detect the error message and to create a custom metric. Associate the Lambda function with the stream. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Configure a CloudWatch alarm to use the custom metric to notify the SNS topic. Subscribe the application team's email address to the SNS topic.

Install the AWS X-Ray daemon on the EC2 instances. Instrument the application with the AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry (ADOT). Configure the ADOT collector with the location of the custom log files and the name of an Amazon CloudWatch log group. Use the CloudWatch embedded metric format to generate a custom metric that is based on the error message. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Configure a CloudWatch alarm to use the custom metric to notify the SNS topic. Subscribe the application team's email address to the SNS topic.

Configure the unified Amazon CloudWatch agent on the EC2 instances to publish the application logs files to a CloudWatch log group. Create an Amazon OpenSearch Service domain. Subscribe the CloudWatch log group to the OpenSearch Service domain. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Configure an OpenSearch Service alert monitor to notify the SNS topic. Subscribe the application team's email address to the SNS topic.

questions.explanation:
The unified CloudWatch agent collects application log files from EC2 instances into a CloudWatch Logs log group, providing centralized storage and search. A metric filter matches each critical error and converts matching log events into a custom CloudWatch metric. A CloudWatch alarm on that metric can publish to an Amazon SNS topic, and an email subscription to that topic sends the alert to the application team. This uses managed native services without requiring custom stream processing, instrumentation, or an additional search cluster.

**Learn more:** [Collect metrics, logs, and traces using the CloudWatch agent](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Install-CloudWatch-Agent.html) · [Creating metrics from log events using filters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/MonitoringLogData.html)

A company has an organization in AWS Organizations. The organization contains workload accounts that host enterprise applications. The company centrally administers users from an operations account. Users cannot be created in the workload accounts. The company recently added an operations team and needs to give its members administrator access to every workload account.  
  
Which combination of actions will provide this access? (Choose three.)

options.text: Create a SysAdmin role in the operations account. Attach the AdministratorAccess policy to the role. Modify the trust relationship to allow the sts:AssumeRole action from the workload accounts.
Create a SysAdmin role in each workload account. Attach the AdministratorAccess policy to the role. Modify the trust relationship to allow the sts:AssumeRole action from the operations account.
Create an Amazon Cognito identity pool in the operations account. Attach the SysAdmin role as an authenticated role.
In the operations account, create an IAM user for each operations team member.

In the operations account, create an IAM user group that is named SysAdmins. Add an IAM policy that allows the sts:AssumeRole action for the SysAdmin role in each workload account. Add all operations team members to the group.
Create an Amazon Cognito user pool in the operations account. Create an Amazon Cognito user for each operations team member.

questions.explanation:
Cross-account IAM access is implemented by creating a role in each workload account, attaching the AdministratorAccess policy to that role, and trusting the operations account in the role’s trust policy. Operations team members need IAM identities in the operations account and an identity-based policy, such as one attached through a group, that allows `sts:AssumeRole` on each workload account’s SysAdmin role. AWS requires both the trusted account’s identity-based permission and the target account role’s trust policy for cross-account role assumption.

**Learn more:** [Cross account resource access in IAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies-cross-account-resource-access.html) · [Grant a user permissions to switch roles](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_use_permissions-to-switch.html)

A company needs to ensure that its EC2 instances are secure. It wants to receive notification when new vulnerabilities are discovered on its instances and to maintain an audit trail of all instance login activity.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS Systems Manager to detect vulnerabilities on the EC2 instances. Install the Amazon Kinesis Agent to capture system logs and deliver them to Amazon S3.
Use AWS Systems Manager to detect vulnerabilities on the EC2 instances. Install the Systems Manager Agent to capture system logs and view login activity in the CloudTrail console.
Configure Amazon CloudWatch to detect vulnerabilities on the EC2 instances. Install the AWS Config daemon to capture system logs and view them in the AWS Config console.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A DevOps engineer finds that every Amazon EC2 instance behind an Application Load Balancer in an Auto Scaling group is not responding to user requests. The EC2 instances are also failing the target group HTTP health checks.  
  
After inspection, the engineer finds that the application process is not running on any EC2 instance. The system logs contain a significant number of out-of-memory messages. The engineer must improve the application's resilience to handle a potential application memory leak. Monitoring and notifications must be enabled to alert when an issue occurs.  
  
Which combination of actions meets these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Change the Auto Scaling configuration to replace the instances when they fail the load balancer's health checks.
Change the target group health check HealthCheckIntervalSeconds parameter to reduce the interval between health checks.
Change the target group health checks from HTTP to TCP to check if the port where the application is listening is reachable.

Enable the available memory consumption metric within the Amazon CloudWatch dashboard for the entire Auto Scaling group. Create an alarm when the memory utilization is high. Associate an Amazon SNS topic to the alarm to receive notifications when the alarm goes off.

A company uses an AWS Organizations organization to manage multiple AWS accounts. The company's development team wants to use AWS Lambda functions to satisfy resiliency requirements and is rewriting all applications to use Lambda functions deployed in a VPC. The development team uses Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) as shared storage in Account A in the organization.  
  
The company wants to keep using Amazon EFS with Lambda. Company policy requires every serverless project to be deployed in Account B.  
  
A DevOps engineer must reconfigure an existing EFS file system so that Lambda functions can access the data through an existing EFS access point.  
  
Which combination of steps should the DevOps engineer take to satisfy these requirements? (Choose three.)

options.text: Update the EFS file system policy to provide Account B with access to mount and write to the EFS file system in Account A.
Create SCPs to set permission guardrails with fine-grained control for Amazon EFS.
Create a new EFS file system in Account B. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to keep data from Account A and Account B synchronized.
Update the Lambda execution roles with permission to access the VPC and the EFS file system. E. Create a VPC peering connection to connect Account A to Account B.
Configure the Lambda functions in Account B to assume an existing IAM role in Account A.

questions.explanation:
An EFS file-system policy in Account A can grant Account B permission to mount and write to the file system. The Lambda execution roles in Account B need EFS client permissions, including `elasticfilesystem:ClientMount` and `elasticfilesystem:ClientWrite`, plus permissions needed to connect to the VPC. A VPC peering connection supplies private network routing between the Lambda VPC and the EFS file system’s VPC so the functions can reach the EFS mount targets.

**Learn more:** [Configuring Amazon EFS file system access - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-filesystem-efs.html) · [Mounting EFS file systems from another VPC - Amazon Elastic File System](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/mount-fs-different-vpc.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An application runs on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. During bootstrapping, the instances register their private IP addresses with a monitoring system. The monitoring system conducts frequent health checks by sending ping requests to those IP addresses and issues alerts when an instance is non-responsive.  
  
The current deployment strategy replaces the existing EC2 instances with new instances. A DevOps Engineer has observed that the monitoring system generates false alarms during deployments and must stop those false alarms.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements without changing the current deployment method?

options.text: Define an Amazon CloudWatch Events target, an AWS Lambda function, and a lifecycle hook attached to the Auto Scaling group. Configure CloudWatch Events to invoke Amazon SNS to send a message to the Systems Administrator group for remediation.

Define an AWS Lambda function and a lifecycle hook attached to the Auto Scaling group. Configure the lifecycle hook to invoke the Lambda function, which removes the entry of the private IP from the monitoring system upon instance termination.

Define an Amazon CloudWatch Events target, an AWS Lambda function, and a lifecycle hook attached to the Auto Scaling group. Configure CloudWatch Events to invoke the Lambda function, which removes the entry of the private IP from the monitoring system upon instance termination.
Define an AWS Lambda function that will run a script when instance termination occurs in an Auto Scaling group. The script will remove the entry of the private IP from the monitoring system.

A company uses AWS Storage Gateway in file gateway mode in front of an Amazon S3 bucket that multiple resources use. In the morning, when business starts, users cannot see the objects that a third party processed the previous evening. When a DevOps engineer checks the S3 bucket directly, the data is present, but it is absent from Storage Gateway.  
  
Which solution makes sure that all updated third-party files are available in the morning?

options.text: Configure a nightly Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) event to trigger an AWS Lambda function to run the RefreshCache command for Storage Gateway.
Instruct the third party to put data into the S3 bucket using AWS Transfer for SFTP.
Modify Storage Gateway to run in volume gateway mode.
Use S3 same-Region replication to replicate any changes made directly in the S3 bucket to Storage Gateway.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 File Gateway does not automatically update its cached object inventory when an external process writes directly to the backing S3 bucket. The `RefreshCache` operation discovers objects that were added, removed, or replaced; scheduling it overnight through EventBridge and Lambda makes the updated inventory available before business hours.

**Learn more:** [Refreshing Amazon S3 bucket object cache](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/refresh-cache.html) · [RefreshCache API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/latest/APIReference/API_RefreshCache.html)

Create an Amazon S3 bucket in us-west-2. Configure server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS) for the S3 bucket. Create and schedule an AWS Lambda function to run weekly to export the CloudWatch logs from the last week to the S3 bucket in us-west-2.

Create and schedule an AWS Lambda function to run weekly to export the CloudWatch logs from the last week to the S3 bucket in us-east-1. Configure a replication rule on the S3 bucket in us-east-1 to replicate the logs to the S3 bucket in us-west-2.

Create and schedule an AWS Lambda function to run weekly to export the CloudWatch logs from the last week to the S3 bucket in us-east-1. Configure a replication rule on the S3 bucket in us-east-1 to replicate the logs to the S3 bucket in us-west-2.

questions.explanation:
Amazon CloudWatch Logs can export to an Amazon S3 bucket only in the same Region as the log data. S3 Cross-Region Replication can then copy the exported objects to `us-west-2`, provided that versioning is enabled on both buckets. Objects encrypted with SSE-S3 replicate with the same encryption type, so the logs remain encrypted in both Regions. SSE-KMS replication requires additional configuration to opt in to replicating KMS-encrypted objects and specify the destination KMS key.

**Learn more:** [Export log data to Amazon S3 using the AWS CLI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/S3ExportTasks.html) · [Replicating encrypted objects (SSE-S3, SSE-KMS, DSSE-KMS, SSE-C)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication-config-for-kms-objects.html)

A company plans to use a grid system for a proprietary enterprise in-memory data store on AWS. The system can run on multiple server nodes in any Linux-based distribution. The system must be able to reconfigure the whole cluster whenever a node is added or removed. When nodes are added or removed, an `/etc/cluster/nodes.config` file must be updated to list the IP addresses of the current node members in that cluster.  
  
The company wants to automate adding new nodes to a cluster.  
  
What can a DevOps engineer do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS OpsWorks Stacks to layer the server nodes of that cluster. Create a Chief recipe that populates the content of the /etc/cluster/nodes.config file and restarts the service by using the current members of the layers. Assign that recipe to the Configure lifecycle event.

Put the file nodes.config in version control. Create an AWS CodeDeploy deployment configuration and deployment group based on an Amazon EC2 tag value for the cluster nodes. When adding a new node to the cluster, update the file with all tagged instances, and make a commit in version control. Deploy the new file and restart the services.

Create an Amazon S3 bucket and upload a version of the /etc/cluster/nodes.config file. Create a crontab script that will poll for that S3 file and download it frequently. Use a process manager, such as Monit or systemd, to restart the cluster services when it detects that the new file was modified. When adding a node to the cluster, edit the file’s most recent members. Upload the new file to the S3 bucket.

Create a user data script that lists all members of the current security group of the cluster and automatically updates the /etc/cluster/nodes.config file whenever a new instance is added to the cluster.

questions.explanation:
AWS OpsWorks Stacks can group cluster servers in a layer and run a custom Chef recipe during the Configure lifecycle event. That event is triggered across the stack when instance membership changes, so the recipe can generate `/etc/cluster/nodes.config` from the current layer members and restart the in-memory data-store service on every node.

**Learn more:** [AWS OpsWorks Stacks Lifecycle Events](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/opsworks/latest/userguide/workingcookbook-events.html)

A DevOps engineer needs to implement an automated response when AWS Trusted Advisor detects an IAM access key in a public source-code repository. The automated response must delete the exposed access key and notify the security team.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an AWS Lambda function to delete the 1AM access key. Configure AWS CloudTrail logs to stream to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Create a CloudWatch Logs metric filter for the AWS_RISK_CREDENTIALS_EXPOSED event with two actions. First, run the Lambda function. Second, use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to send a notification to the security team.
Create an AWS Lambda function to delete the IAM access key. Create an AWS Config rule for changes to

Create an AWS Lambda function that deletes the IAM access key and then uses Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to notify the security team. Create an AWS Personal Health Dashboard rule for the AWS_RISK_CREDENTIALS_EXPOSED event. Set the target of the Personal Health Dashboard rule to the ARN of the Lambda function.
Create an AWS Lambda function that deletes the IAM access key. Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule with an

questions.explanation:
AWS Trusted Advisor publishes its Exposed Access Keys check result as an event (source aws.trustedadvisor) to the default Amazon EventBridge event bus. Creating an EventBridge rule that matches the 'aws.trustedadvisor' source with the 'Exposed Access Keys' status and targets both a Lambda function (which deletes the exposed IAM access key) and an SNS topic (which notifies the security team) is the correct, fully event-driven solution. Option A is wrong because Trusted Advisor does not emit AWS_RISK_CREDENTIALS_EXPOSED into CloudTrail/CloudWatch Logs for a metric filter to catch; option B misuses AWS Config (which evaluates resource configuration, not Trusted Advisor events); option C misuses the Personal Health Dashboard, which is not the event source for this check.

**Learn more:** [Auto-remediate best-practice deviations detected by AWS Trusted Advisor](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/mt/auto-remediate-best-practice-deviations-detected-by-aws-trusted-advisor/) · [Reduce risk with the Trusted Advisor exposed access keys recommendation](https://repost.aws/articles/ARSdqO8fHQTYKry6D_U9lytQ/reduce-your-security-risk-with-aws-trusted-advisor-exposed-access-keys-recommendation)

A United States–based online retail company plans to expand its operations into Europe and Asia within the next six months. Its product currently runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. All data is stored in an Amazon Aurora database instance.  
  
When the product is deployed across multiple Regions, the company requires one product catalog shared by all Regions; however, for compliance reasons, customer information and purchases must remain in each Region.  
  
How should the company satisfy these requirements with the **LEAST** application changes?

options.text: Use Amazon Redshift for the product catalog and Amazon DynamoDB tables for the customer information and purchases.
Use Amazon DynamoDB global tables for the product catalog and regional tables for the customer information and purchases.
Use Aurora with read replicas for the product catalog and additional local Aurora instances in each region for the customer information and purchases.
Use Aurora for the product catalog and Amazon DynamoDB global tables for the customer information and purchases.

questions.explanation:
The application already stores all data in Amazon Aurora, and the decisive requirement is the LEAST application changes. Keeping Aurora for both data sets minimizes code changes: use Aurora cross-region read replicas (Aurora global database) so the single product catalog is written in the primary Region and read locally in every Region, and stand up an independent local Aurora database in each Region so customer information and purchases remain in-Region for compliance. Options B and D move data to Amazon DynamoDB, which forces a rewrite of the data-access layer (a large application change), and DynamoDB global tables replicate data across Regions, which would violate the requirement that customer data stay within each Region.

**Learn more:** [Amazon Aurora global databases](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-global-database.html) · [Working with Aurora read replicas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-replication.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A development team uses AWS CodeDeploy blue/green deployments to manage website releases. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer.  
  
When a new revision is deployed, the team finds that the deployment eventually fails, but only after a lengthy delay. Further investigation shows that the `AllowTraffic` lifecycle event ran for one hour and then failed without any additional information. The team needs failure notifications to arrive sooner while preserving application availability even if the deployment fails.  
  
Which combination of actions should be taken to satisfy these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Change the deployment configuration to CodeDeployDefault.AllAtOnce to speed up the deployment process by deploying to all of the instances at the same time.
Create a CodeDeploy trigger for the deployment failure event and make the deployment fail as soon as a single health check failure is detected.
Reduce the HealthCheckIntervalSeconds and UnhealthyThresholdCount values within the target group health checks to decrease the amount of time it takes for the application to be considered unhealthy.
Use the appspec.yml file to run a script on the AllowTraffic hook to perform lighter health checks on the application instead of making CodeDeploy wait for the target group health checks to pass.

Use the appspec.yml file to run a script on the BeforeAllowTraffic hook to perform health checks on the application and fail the deployment if the health checks performed by the script are not successful.

questions.explanation:
Application Load Balancer target-group health checks use `HealthCheckIntervalSeconds` as the interval between checks and `UnhealthyThresholdCount` as the number of consecutive failures required to mark a target unhealthy. Reducing both values shortens detection of an unhealthy replacement target. For EC2 blue/green deployments, `BeforeAllowTraffic` supports AppSpec scripts before the replacement instances are registered with the load balancer, so a failed health-check script stops the deployment before production traffic is sent to the replacement environment. `AllowTraffic` itself is reserved for CodeDeploy operations and cannot run scripts.

**Learn more:** [Troubleshoot EC2/On-Premises deployment issues — AWS CodeDeploy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/troubleshooting-deployments.html) · [AppSpec 'hooks' section — AWS CodeDeploy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/reference-appspec-file-structure-hooks.html)

A company runs a multi-tenant application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The instances use Windows Server and belong to an Auto Scaling group. The application relies on a license file on the instances that can be updated without disrupting customers. When a new customer buys access to the application, the company’s licensing team adds a new license key to a file in an Amazon S3 bucket. After the license file is updated, the operations team manually updates the EC2 instances.  
  
A DevOps engineer must automate the EC2 instance file-update process. The automated process must reduce the time it takes EC2 instances to receive the updated license file and must notify the operations team whether the update process succeeds or fails.  
  
The DevOps engineer creates a resource group in AWS Resource Groups. The resource group uses a tag that the Auto Sealing group applies to the EC2 instances.  
  
What should the DevOps engineer do next to meet the requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?

options.text: Create an S3 event notification to invoke an AWS Lambda function when the license file is updated in the S3 bucket. Configure the Lambda function to invoke AWS Systems Manager Run Command to run the AWS-RunRemoteScript document to download the updated license file. Specify the command from Lambda to run on the application's resource group with 50% concurrency. Configure Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) notifications for event notifications of SUCCESS and FAILED to send email notifications to the operations team.

Create an S3 event notification to invoke an AWS Lambda function when the license file is updated in the S3 bucket. Configure the Lambda function to invoke AWS Systems Manager Run Command to run the AWS-RunPowerShellScript document to download the updated license file. Specify the command from Lambda to run on the application's resource group with 50% concurrency. Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to send event notifications of SUCCESS and FAILED. Subscribe the email addresses of the operations team members to the SNS topic.

Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule that runs each hour to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to invoke AWS Systems Manager Run Command to run the AWS-RunPowerShellScript document to download the updated license file. Specify the command from Lambda to run on the application's resource group with 50% concurrency. Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to send event notifications of SUCCESS and FAILED. Subscribe the email addresses of the operations team members to the SNS topic.

Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule that runs each hour to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to invoke AWS Systems Manager Run Command to run the AWS-RunRemoteScript document to download the updated license file. Specify the command from Lambda to run on the application's resource group with 50% concurrency. Configure Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) notifications for event notifications of SUCCESS and FAILED to send email notifications to the operations team.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon S3 event notification invokes processing as soon as the license file changes, avoiding the delay of scheduled polling. AWS Systems Manager Run Command can target a resource group and use percentage-based concurrency; on Windows instances, AWS-RunPowerShellScript runs the download command. Run Command sends command-status notifications, including Success and Failed, to an Amazon SNS topic, which can deliver them by email to the operations team.

**Learn more:** [Use Run Command to send a command that returns status notifications](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/monitoring-sns-rc-send.html) · [Walkthrough: Use AWS Tools for Windows PowerShell with Run Command](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/walkthrough-powershell.html)

A DevOps Engineer operates a large commercial website running on Amazon EC2. The website uses Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to gather and process web logs. The DevOps Engineer also manages the Kinesis consumer application, which runs on Amazon EC2.  
  
Unexpected data spikes cause the Kinesis consumer application to lag, and the Kinesis data streams discard records before they are processed. The DevOps Engineer must implement a solution that improves stream handling.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements with the **MOST** operational efficiency?

options.text: Modify the Kinesis consumer application to store the logs durably in Amazon S3. Use Amazon EMR to process the data directly on Amazon S3 to derive customer insights. Store the results in Amazon S3.

Horizontally scale the Kinesis consumer application by adding more EC2 instances based on the Amazon CloudWatch GetRecords.IteratorAgeMilliseconds metric. Increase the retention period of the Kinesis Data Streams.
Convert the Kinesis consumer application to run as an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Kinesis Data Streams as the event source for the Lambda function to process the data streams.
Increase the number of shards in the Kinesis Data Streams to increase the overall throughput so that the consumer application processes data faster.

questions.explanation:
AWS Lambda can consume Amazon Kinesis Data Streams through an event source mapping. Lambda polls stream shards, invokes the function with batches of records, and provides managed event-driven scaling, eliminating the operational work of provisioning and scaling EC2 consumer instances. Lambda can also increase concurrent batches per shard with the event source mapping parallelization setting when stream volume is volatile and IteratorAge is high.

**Learn more:** [Using Lambda to process records from Amazon Kinesis Data Streams](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-kinesis.html) · [Process Amazon Kinesis Data Streams records with Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-kinesis-create.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A DevOps Engineer needs to monitor the health of a stateless RESTful service behind a Classic Load Balancer. New application revisions are deployed through a CI/CD pipeline. If the service latency rises above a defined threshold, the deployment must stop until the service recovers.  
  
Which of the following approaches provides the **QUICKEST** detection time?

options.text: Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics provided by Elastic Load Balancing to calculate average latency. Alarm and stop deployment when latency increases beyond the defined threshold.
Use AWS Lambda and Elastic Load Balancing access logs to detect average latency. Alarm and stop deployment when latency increases beyond the defined threshold.
Use AWS CodeDeploy's MinimumHealthyHosts setting to define thresholds for rolling back deployments. If these thresholds are breached, roll back the deployment.
Use Metric Filters to parse application logs in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Create a filter for latency. Alarm and stop deployment when latency increases beyond the defined threshold.

questions.explanation:
A Classic Load Balancer publishes the native `AWS/ELB` `Latency` metric to Amazon CloudWatch in 60-second intervals when requests are flowing. Its `Average` statistic directly measures the required average latency, so a CloudWatch alarm can promptly trigger an action to stop the deployment. Access-log processing adds delivery and processing delay; minimum healthy-host settings do not measure latency; and application-log filters depend on application logging and log ingestion.

**Learn more:** [CloudWatch metrics for your Classic Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/classic/elb-cloudwatch-metrics.html) · [Monitor your Classic Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/classic/elb-monitor-logs.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company needs to obtain user consent for a privacy agreement. The company deploys an application across six AWS Regions: two Regions in North America, two Regions in Europe, and two Regions in Asia. The application has a user base of 20 million to 30 million users.  
  
The company must read and write data related to each user's response. The company must also make sure that the responses are available in all six Regions.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LOWEST** read and write latency?

options.text: Implement Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) in each of the six Regions.
Implement Amazon DynamoDB global tables in each of the six Regions.
Implement Amazon ElastiCache for Redis replication groups in each of the six Regions.
Implement Amazon Elasticsearch Service (Amazon ES) in each of the six Regions.

questions.explanation:
Amazon DynamoDB global tables automatically replicate data among regional replicas, and every replica can serve reads and writes. Routing users to a nearby replica provides fast local read and write performance while making consent-response data available across all six Regions.

**Learn more:** [Global tables - multi-active, multi-Region replication - Amazon DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/GlobalTables.html) · [Using DynamoDB global tables - Amazon DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/bp-global-table-design.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ecommerce company wants to deploy an application on AWS that meets these requirements:  
  
- Provides a simple, automated application-deployment process.  
- Keeps deployment costs minimal while ensuring that at least half of the instances remain available to receive end-user requests.  
- Replaces affected instances through an automated healing mechanism if the application fails.  
  
Which deployment strategy satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Create an AWS Elastic Beanstalk environment and configure it to use Auto Scaling and an Elastic Load Balancer. Use rolling deployments with a batch size of 50%.
Create an AWS OpsWorks stack. Configure the application layer to use rolling deployments as a deployment strategy. Add an Elastic Load Balancing layer. Enable auto healing on the application layer.

Use AWS CodeDeploy with Auto Scaling and an Elastic Load Balancer. Use the CodeDeployDefault.HalfAtAtime deployment strategy. Enable an Elastic Load Balancing health check to report the status of the application, and set the Auto Scaling health check to ELB.

Use AWS CodeDeploy with Auto Scaling and an Elastic Load Balancer. Use a blue/green deployment strategy. Enable an Elastic Load Balancing health check to report the status of the application, and set the Auto Scaling health check to ELB.

questions.explanation:
`CodeDeployDefault.HalfAtATime` deploys to no more than half of the instances at once, retaining at least half as healthy hosts during an in-place deployment and avoiding the duplicate environment required for a blue/green deployment. Configuring the Auto Scaling group to use Elastic Load Balancing health checks causes instances reported unhealthy by the load balancer to be marked unhealthy and replaced automatically.

**Learn more:** [Working with deployment configurations in CodeDeploy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/deployment-configurations.html) · [About the health checks for your Auto Scaling group](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/health-checks-overview.html)
