lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A DevOps Engineer manages an application for a video-production company that handles video files. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an ELB Application Load Balancer. The instances are in an Auto Scaling group spanning multiple Availability Zones. Data is stored in an Amazon RDS PostgreSQL Multi-AZ DB instance, and video files are kept in an Amazon S3 bucket. On a typical day, 50 GB of new video is added to the S3 bucket. The Engineer must implement a multi-Region disaster recovery plan that provides the least data loss and the lowest recovery times. The existing application infrastructure is already defined by using AWS CloudFormation.  
  
Which deployment option should the Engineer select to meet the system's uptime and recovery objectives?

options.text: Launch the application from the CloudFormation template in the second region, which sets the capacity of the Auto Scaling group to 1. Create an Amazon RDS read replica in the second region. In the second region, enable cross-region replication between the original S3 bucket and a new S3 bucket. To fail over, promote the read replica as master. Update the CloudFormation stack and increase the capacity of the Auto Scaling group.

Launch the application from the CloudFormation template in the second region, which sets the capacity of the Auto Scaling group to 1. Create a scheduled task to take daily Amazon RDS cross-region snapshots to the second region. In the second region, enable cross-region replication between the original S3 bucket and Amazon Glacier. In a disaster, launch a new application stack in the second region and restore the database from the most recent snapshot.

Launch the application from the CloudFormation template in the second region, which sets the capacity of the Auto Scaling group to 1. Use Amazon CloudWatch Events to schedule a nightly task to take a snapshot of the database, copy the snapshot to the second region, and replace the DB instance in the second region from the snapshot. In the second region, enable cross-region replication between the original S3 bucket and a new S3 bucket. To fail over, increase the capacity of the Auto Scaling group.

Use Amazon CloudWatch Events to schedule a nightly task to take a snapshot of the database and copy the snapshot to the second region. Create an AWS Lambda function that copies each object to a new S3 bucket in the second region in response to S3 event notifications. In the second region, launch the application from the CloudFormation template and restore the database from the most recent snapshot.

questions.explanation:
A cross-Region RDS for PostgreSQL read replica is kept current through replication and can be promoted to a standalone writable DB instance during recovery. S3 Cross-Region Replication automatically and asynchronously copies new and updated objects to a bucket in another Region. Keeping a minimal application stack running in the recovery Region allows capacity to be increased during failover, avoiding the delay and data-loss exposure of restoring periodic snapshots.

**Learn more:** [Creating a read replica in a different AWS Region - Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.XRgn.html) · [Working with read replicas for Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_PostgreSQL.Replication.ReadReplicas.html)

A DevOps team operates an on-premises API that functions as the backend for an Amazon API Gateway endpoint. Customers have reported high response latency, which the development team has confirmed by using the API Gateway latency metrics in Amazon CloudWatch. To determine the cause, the team must gather relevant data without adding latency.  
  
Which actions should be taken to achieve this? (Choose two.)

options.text: Install the CloudWatch agent server side and configure the agent to upload relevant logs to CloudWatch.
Enable AWS X-Ray tracing in API Gateway, modify the application to capture request segments, and upload those segments to X-Ray during each request.
Enable AWS X-Ray tracing in API Gateway, modify the application to capture request segments, and use the X-Ray daemon to upload segments to X-Ray.
Modify the on-premises application to send log information back to API Gateway with each request.
Modify the on-premises application to calculate and upload statistical data relevant to the API service requests to CloudWatch metrics.

questions.explanation:
The CloudWatch agent can collect relevant server-side log data outside the request-processing path. The AWS X-Ray daemon receives application trace segments locally and uploads them asynchronously, avoiding direct segment uploads during each API request and minimizing added request latency.

**Learn more:** [Set up AWS X-Ray with API Gateway REST APIs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-enabling-xray.html) · [Installing the CloudWatch agent](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/install-CloudWatch-Agent-on-EC2-Instance.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Application Load Balancers (ALBs) within its application architecture. The company has ALBs in AWS accounts that belong to an organization in AWS Organizations. AWS Config is configured in every AWS account in the organization.  
  
The company must apply an AWS WAF web ACL containing a common rule set to every ALB, including ALBs created in the future. Administrators in each AWS account must be able to define their own AWS WAF rules in addition to the common rules provided by the company’s security team for all accounts.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure AWS Firewall Manager for the organization. In the Firewall Manager administrator account, create an AWS WAF policy. Turn on automatic remediation and define the web ACL. Configure the policy scope to apply to all ALBs in the organization.

Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) from the organization's management account to enable resource sharing in the organization. Create the web ACL. Configure a resource share of the web ACL for the organization. Associate the shared web ACL with all the ALBs in the organization.

Set up the ALB_WAF_ENABLED AWS Config managed rule with automatic remediation. Configure the rule to create the web ACL and to attach the web ACL to all ALBs in an AWS account. Create an AWS Config conformance pack that contains the rule. Deploy the conformance pack to all AWS accounts in the organization.

Configure AWS Firewall Manager for the organization. In the Firewall Manager administrator account, create an AWS WAF policy that defines the web ACL. Set up the ALB_WAF_ENABLED AWS Config managed rule with automatic remediation. Configure the rule to attach the web ACL to all ALBs in an AWS account. Deploy the rule to all AWS accounts in the organization.

questions.explanation:
AWS Firewall Manager can enforce an AWS WAF policy across all in-scope ALBs in an AWS Organization and automatically applies the policy to newly added resources. Firewall Manager creates and manages web ACLs containing the centrally defined rule groups, while member-account administrators can add their own rules and rule groups to those web ACLs.

**Learn more:** [Using AWS WAF policies with Firewall Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-policies.html) · [Using the AWS Firewall Manager policy scope](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/policy-scope.html)

A company uses an Amazon API Gateway API and an AWS Lambda function to host a microservice. The microservice retrieves pricing data from an Amazon DynamoDB table for the company’s online store.  
  
Interest in the online store has grown. Consequently, latency issues and throttling occur on the DynamoDB table when a particular query runs. Some internal services access the DynamoDB table directly. The current solution has no caching enabled.  
  
A DevOps engineer observes that repeated API requests take the same amount of time as unique requests. The DevOps engineer must reduce latency for repeated API requests and reduce throttling on the DynamoDB table.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Enable caching for API Gateway stages. Use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) for the DynamoDB table.
Enable caching tor API Gateway stages. Use Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached caching for the DynamoDB table.
Use provisioned concurrency for the Lambda function. Use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) for the DynamoDB table.
Use provisioned concurrency for the Lambda function. Increase the RCUs for the DynamoDB table.

questions.explanation:
API Gateway stage caching stores endpoint responses and serves cache hits without invoking the endpoint, which lowers latency for repeated API requests. DAX is a DynamoDB-compatible in-memory cache that serves repeated, eventually consistent reads with microsecond latency and offloads those reads from the underlying DynamoDB table, reducing read-capacity pressure and throttling.

**Learn more:** [Cache settings for REST APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-caching.html) · [In-memory acceleration with DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/DAX.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A DevOps engineer at a company supports an AWS environment where all users use AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On). The company wants to immediately disable the credentials of every newly created IAM user and have the security team receive a notification.  
  
Which combination of steps should the DevOps engineer take to satisfy these requirements? (Choose three.)

options.text: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to an IAM CreateUser API call in AWS CloudTrail.
Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to an IAM GetLoginProfile API call in AWS CloudTrail.
Create an AWS Lambda function that is a target of the EventBridge rule. Configure the Lambda function to disable any access keys and delete the login profiles that are associated with the IAM user.
Create an AWS Lambda function that is a target of the EventBridge rule. Configure the Lambda function to delete the login profiles that are associated with the IAM user.
Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic that is a target of the EventBridge rule. Subscribe the security team’s group email address to the topic.
Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue that is a target of the Lambda function. Subscribe the security team's group email address to the queue.

questions.explanation:
IAM service API activity can be matched in Amazon EventBridge through AWS CloudTrail, including a specific `CreateUser` operation. Removing an IAM user's login profile deletes that user's password, but it does not prevent CLI or API access; any access keys must also be made inactive or deleted. Amazon SNS supports email subscriptions and can be an EventBridge rule target, enabling notification of the security team's group email address.

**Learn more:** [AWS Identity and Access Management events - Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/ref/events-ref-iam.html) · [DeleteLoginProfile - AWS Identity and Access Management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/APIReference/API_DeleteLoginProfile.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses AWS Organizations to create separate AWS accounts for each department. The company must automate these tasks:  
  
- Periodically update Linux AMIs with new patches and produce a golden image.  
- Install a newer version of Chef agents in the golden image, when available.  
- Make the newly created AMIs available to the departments’ accounts.  
  
Which solution fulfills these requirements with the **LEAST** management overhead?

options.text: Write a script to launch an Amazon EC2 instance from the previous golden image. Apply the patch updates. Install the new version of the Chef agent, generate a new golden image, and then modify the AMI permissions to share only the new image with the department's accounts.

Use Amazon EC2 Image Builder to create an image pipeline that consists of the base Linux AMI and components to install the Chef agent. Use AWS Resource Access Manager to share EC2 Image Builder images with the department's accounts.

Use an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook to update the Linux AMI by using the previous image. Provide the URL for the script that will update the Chef agent. Use AWS Organizations to replace the previous golden image in the department's accounts.

Use Amazon EC2 Image Builder to create an image pipeline that consists of the base Linux AMI and components to install the Chef agent. Create a parameter in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store to store the new AMI ID that can be referenced by the department's accounts.

questions.explanation:
EC2 Image Builder provides a managed image pipeline that automatically builds a hardened, patched golden AMI from a base Linux image plus components (for example, one that installs the Chef agent), on a schedule and with minimal management overhead. EC2 Image Builder integrates natively with AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM), which can share Image Builder images, components, and recipes with other accounts or across an AWS Organization, making the resulting AMIs available to the department accounts. Option A is a hand-maintained script with manual sharing (high overhead). Option D also uses Image Builder but only stores the AMI ID in Parameter Store — storing an ID does not grant the other accounts permission to launch the AMI, so the image is not actually shared.

**Learn more:** [Share Image Builder resources with AWS RAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/imagebuilder/latest/userguide/manage-shared-resources.html) · [What is EC2 Image Builder](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/imagebuilder/latest/userguide/what-is-image-builder.html)

A company uses Amazon EC2 for multiple workloads. Company policy requires instances to be centrally managed in order to standardize configurations. These configurations include standard logging, metrics, security assessments, and weekly patching.  
  
How can the company satisfy these requirements? (Choose three.)

options.text: Use AWS Config to ensure all EC2 instances are managed by Amazon Inspector.
Use AWS Config to ensure all EC2 instances are managed by AWS Systems Manager.
Use AWS Systems Manager to install and manage Amazon Inspector, Systems Manager Patch Manager, and the Amazon CloudWatch agent on all instances.
Use Amazon Inspector to install and manage AWS Systems Manager, Systems Manager Patch Manager, and the Amazon CloudWatch agent on all instances.

Use AWS Systems Manager maintenance windows with Systems Manager Run Command to schedule Systems Manager Patch Manager tasks. Use the Amazon CloudWatch agent to schedule Amazon Inspector assessment runs.

Use AWS Systems Manager maintenance windows with Systems Manager Run Command to schedule Systems Manager Patch Manager tasks. Use Amazon CloudWatch Events to schedule Amazon Inspector assessment runs.

questions.explanation:
AWS Config includes a managed rule for checking whether EC2 instances are managed by AWS Systems Manager. Systems Manager provides centralized management and can deploy the CloudWatch agent to managed nodes. Systems Manager Maintenance Windows can run scheduled Run Command patch tasks, while Amazon Inspector Classic schedules recurring assessment runs by creating an Amazon CloudWatch Events rule. The CloudWatch agent collects logs and metrics; it does not schedule Inspector assessments.

**Learn more:** [AWS Config managed rules](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/managed-rules-by-aws-config.html) · [AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/patch-manager.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates several applications across multiple AWS accounts within an AWS Organizations organization. Some resources are improperly tagged, and the finance team cannot identify which costs belong to which applications. A DevOps engineer must correct this problem and ensure it does not recur.  
  
Which combination of actions should the DevOps engineer take to satisfy these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Activate the user-defined cost allocation tags in each AWS account.
Create and attach an SCP that requires a specific tag.
Define each line of business (LOB) in AWS Budgets. Assign the required tag to each resource.
Scan all accounts with Tag Editor. Assign the required tag to each resource.
Use the budget report to find untagged resources. Assign the required tag to each resource.

questions.explanation:
AWS Tag Editor can find and apply tags to supported existing resources, remediating the current untagged-resource population. An AWS Organizations service control policy can use an explicit deny with an `aws:RequestTag` condition to require a tag during supported resource-creation requests, preventing future resources from being created without that tag. User-defined cost-allocation tag activation is controlled centrally by the organization’s management account rather than independently in each member account.

**Learn more:** [Using user-defined cost allocation tags](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/custom-tags.html) · [Guidance for Tagging on AWS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/solutions/tagging-on-aws/)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company gives external users access to its AWS account by creating an IAM user for every external user. A DevOps engineer must implement a solution that revokes access for IAM users that have not accessed the account for 90 days.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Turn on AWS Config in the AWS account. Deploy the lam-user-unused-credentials-check AWS Config managed rule Configure the rule to run periodically Configure AWS. Config automatic remediation to run the AWSConfigRemediation-RevokeUnusedlAMUserCredentials AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook.

Use AWS Identity and Access Management Access Analyzer to create an analyzer in the AWS account. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to match IAM Access Analyzer events for IAM users that were last accessed more than 90 days ago. Configure the rule to run the AWSConfigRemediation-DetachlAMPolicy AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook to detach any policies that are attached to the IAM user.

Enable AWS Trusted Advisor in the AWS account. Use the AWS Developer Support plan to access the AWS Support API. Configure an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule to use the Support API’s Trusted Advisor IAM Access Key Rotation check to discover IAM credentials that have not been accessed for more than 90 days. Configure another EventBridge rule to use the Trusted Advisor Check Item Refresh Status event type and to run the AWSConfigRemediation-RevokeUnusedlAMUserCredentials AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook.

Enable AWS Security Hub in the AWS account. Configure a Security Hub rule that determines when an IAM user was last accessed. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule to match the Security Hub rule and to run the AWSConfigRemediation-RevokeUnusedlAMUserCredentials AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook.

questions.explanation:
The AWS Config managed rule `iam-user-unused-credentials-check` periodically identifies IAM users whose passwords or active access keys have not been used within the configured number of days; its default threshold is 90 days. AWS Config automatic remediation can invoke the `AWSConfigRemediation-RevokeUnusedIAMUserCredentials` Systems Manager Automation runbook, which revokes unused IAM passwords and active access keys.

**Learn more:** [iam-user-unused-credentials-check - AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/iam-user-unused-credentials-check.html) · [AWSConfigRemediation-RevokeUnusedIAMUserCredentials - AWS Systems Manager Automation Runbook Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager-automation-runbooks/latest/userguide/automation-aws-revoke-iam-user.html)

An Engineering team operates a Node.js e-commerce application. The current environment includes:  
  
- Amazon S3 buckets to store content  
- Amazon EC2 for the front-end web servers  
- AWS Lambda for image processing  
- Amazon DynamoDB to store session-related data  
  
The team anticipates a substantial increase in site traffic. The application must accommodate the extra load without interruption. Initial testing added new servers to the EC2 front end for the greater load, but the instances required up to 20 minutes to become completely configured. The team wants to shorten this configuration time.  
  
Which changes must the Engineering team implement to make the solution the **MOST** resilient and highly available while satisfying the expected increase in demand?

options.text: Use AWS OpsWorks to automatically configure each new EC2 instance as it is launched. Configure the EC2 instances by using an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer across multiple Availability Zones. Implement Amazon DynamoDB Auto Scaling. Use Amazon Route 53 to point the application DNS record to the Application Load Balancer.

Deploy a fleet of EC2 instances, doubling the current capacity, and place them behind an Application Load Balancer. Increase the Amazon DynamoDB read and write capacity units. Add an alias record that contains the Application Load Balancer endpoint to the existing Amazon Route 53 DNS record that points to the application.

Configure Amazon CloudFront and have its origin point to Amazon S3 to host the web application. Implement Amazon DynamoDB Auto Scaling. Use Amazon Route 53 to point the application DNS record to the CloudFront DNS name.

Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk with a custom AMI including all web components. Deploy the platform by using an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer across multiple Availability Zones. Implement Amazon DynamoDB Auto Scaling. Use Amazon Route 53 to point the application DNS record to the Elastic Beanstalk load balancer.

questions.explanation:
A custom AMI containing the web components removes most launch-time configuration work, allowing new EC2 instances to become available quickly. An Elastic Beanstalk environment can use Auto Scaling and an Application Load Balancer across multiple Availability Zones for resilient, horizontally scalable web capacity. DynamoDB Auto Scaling adjusts provisioned read and write capacity in response to traffic, and Route 53 can direct the application DNS record to the Elastic Beanstalk load balancer.

**Learn more:** [Using a custom Amazon machine image (AMI) in your Elastic Beanstalk environment](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/using-features.customenv.html) · [Auto Scaling your Elastic Beanstalk environment instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/using-features.managing.as.html)

A DevOps engineer uses AWS CodeDeploy across a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances in an EC2 Auto Scaling group. The related CodeDeploy deployment group is integrated with EC2 Auto Scaling and configured for in-place deployments using `CodeDeplcyDefault.OneAtATime`.  
  
During a new deployment that is in progress, the engineer finds that, although the overall deployment completed successfully, two of five instances have the prior application revision. The remaining three instances have the latest application revision.  
  
What is the likely cause of this issue?

options.text: The two affected instances failed to fetch the new deployment.
A failed AfterInstall lifecycle event hook caused the CodeDeploy agent to roll back to the previous version on the affected instances.
The CodeDeploy agent was not installed in two affected instances.
EC2 Auto Scaling launched two new instances while the new deployment had not yet finished, causing the previous version to be deployed on the affected instances.

questions.explanation:
When an EC2 Auto Scaling scale-out event occurs while a CodeDeploy deployment is underway, the newly launched instances receive the previously deployed application revision rather than the revision currently being deployed. This can leave the original and newly scaled-out instances on different revisions after a successful deployment.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company grants its employees limited AWS permissions. DevOps engineers can assume an administrator role. For audit tracking, the security team needs a near-real-time notification whenever the administrator role is assumed.  
  
How should this be achieved?

options.text: Configure AWS Config to publish logs to an Amazon S3 bucket. Use Amazon Athena to query the logs and send a notification to the security team when the administrator role is assumed.
Configure Amazon GuardDuty to monitor when the administrator role is assumed and send a notification to the security team.

Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) event rule using an AWS Management Console sign-in events event pattern that publishes a message to an Amazon SNS topic if the administrator role is assumed.

Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) events rule using an AWS API call that uses an AWS CloudTrail event pattern to trigger an AWS Lambda function that publishes a message to an Amazon SNS topic if the administrator role is assumed.

questions.explanation:
AWS STS role assumption is an `AssumeRole` API operation. AWS CloudTrail delivers matching API-call events to the default Amazon EventBridge event bus, where an EventBridge rule can filter for the STS `AssumeRole` event and the administrator role. The rule can invoke AWS Lambda, which publishes the notification to an Amazon SNS topic.

**Learn more:** [AWS Security Token Service events - Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/ref/events-ref-sts.html) · [AWS service events delivered via AWS CloudTrail - Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-service-event-cloudtrail.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company requires that every Amazon EC2 instance be launched from an AMI produced by the company's security team. Each month, the security team emails all development teams with the latest approved AMIs.  
  
The development teams deploy their applications by using AWS CloudFormation. When developers launch a new service, they must search their email for the latest AMIs sent by the security department. A DevOps engineer wants to automate the process the security team uses to provide AMI IDs to the development teams.  
  
What is the **MOST scalable** solution that meets these requirements?

options.text: Direct the security team to use CloudFormation to create new versions of the AMIs and to list the AMI ARNs in an encrypted Amazon S3 object as part of the stack's Outputs section. Instruct the developers to use a cross-stack reference to load the encrypted S3 object and obtain the most recent AMI ARNs.

Direct the security team to use a CloudFormation stack to create an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that builds new AMIs and places the latest AMI ARNs in an encrypted Amazon S3 object as part of the pipeline output. Instruct the developers to use a cross-stack reference within their own CloudFormation template to obtain the S3 object location and the most recent AMI ARNs.

Direct the security team to use Amazon EC2 Image Builder to create new AMIs and to place the AMI ARNs as parameters in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Instruct the developers to specify a parameter of type SSM in their CloudFormation stack to obtain the most recent AMI ARNs from Parameter Store.

Direct the security team to use Amazon EC2 Image Builder to create new AMIs and to create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic so that every development team can receive notifications. When the development teams receive a notification, instruct them to write an AWS Lambda function that will update their CloudFormation stack with the most recent AMI ARNs.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EC2 Image Builder can distribute a newly built AMI by updating an AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store parameter. A CloudFormation parameter such as `AWS::SSM::Parameter::Value<AWS::EC2::Image::Id>` retrieves the current parameter value for stack operations, so teams can consistently use the centrally approved AMI without manual email searches or per-team automation.

**Learn more:** [Specify existing resources at runtime with CloudFormation-supplied parameter types](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/cloudformation-supplied-parameter-types.html) · [AWS::ImageBuilder::DistributionConfiguration SsmParameterConfiguration](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-properties-imagebuilder-distributionconfiguration-ssmparameterconfiguration.html)

The company has configured an Amazon CloudFront distribution that uses the S3 bucket as its origin. Web clients download the SDK through the CloudFront distribution endpoint. A DevOps engineer must implement a solution that automatically makes the new SDK available during new API deployments.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a CodePipeline action immediately after the deployment stage of the API. Configure the action to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to download the SDK from API Gateway, upload the SDK to the S3 bucket, and create a CloudFront invalidation for the SDK path.

Create a CodePipeline action immediately after the deployment stage of the API. Configure the action to use the CodePipeline integration with API Gateway to export the SDK to Amazon S3. Configure the rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function to download the SDK from API Gateway, upload the SDK to the S3 bucket, and call the CloudFront API to create an invalidation for the SDK path.

Configure the rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function to download the SDK from API Gateway, upload the SDK to the S3 bucket, and call the S3 API to invalidate the cache for the SDK path.

questions.explanation:

The security team relies on AWS CloudTrail to detect sensitive security issues in the company’s AWS account. The DevOps engineer needs a solution that automatically remediates CloudTrail being turned off in an AWS account.  
  
Which solution provides the **LEAST** downtime for CloudTrail log deliveries?

options.text: Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule for the CloudTrail StopLogging event. Create an AWS Lambda function that uses the AWS SDK to call StartLogging on the ARN of the resource in which StopLogging was called. Add the Lambda function ARN as a target to the EventBridge (CloudWatch Events) rule.

Deploy the AWS-managed CloudTrail-enabled AWS Config rule, set with a periodic interval of 1 hour. Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule for AWS Config rules compliance change. Create an AWS Lambda function that uses the AWS SDK to call StartLogging on the ARN of the resource in which StopLogging was called. Add the Lambda function ARN as a target to the EventBridge (CloudWatch Events) rule.

Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule for a scheduled event every 5 minutes. Create an AWS Lambda function that uses the AWS SDK to call StartLogging on a CloudTrail trail in the AWS account. Add the Lambda function ARN as a target to the EventBridge (CloudWatch Events) rule.

Launch a t2.nano instance with a script running every 5 minutes that uses the AWS SDK to query CloudTrail in the current account. If the CloudTrail trail is disabled, have the script re-enable the trail.

questions.explanation:
An EventBridge rule can react to the `StopLogging` API call recorded by CloudTrail and immediately invoke a Lambda function. The function can call `StartLogging` on the affected trail ARN, which resumes recording AWS API calls and log-file delivery. This event-driven response minimizes the interruption compared with periodic AWS Config or scheduled five-minute checks.

**Learn more:** [AWS CloudTrail events - Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/ref/events-ref-cloudtrail.html) · [StartLogging - AWS CloudTrail API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/APIReference/API_StartLogging.html)

options.text: Use the cfn-signal helper script to signal success or failure to CloudFormation. Use the WaitOnResourceSignals update policy within the CloudFormation template. Set an appropriate timeout for the update policy.

Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for the UnhealthyHostCount metric. Include an appropriate alarm threshold for the target group. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic as the target to signal success or failure to CloudFormation.

Create a lifecycle hook on the Auto Scaling group by using the AWS::AutoScaling::LifecycleHook resource. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic as the target to signal success or failure to CloudFormation. Set an appropriate timeout on the lifecycle hook.

Use the Amazon CloudWatch agent to stream the cloud-init logs. Create a subscription filter that includes an AWS Lambda function with an appropriate invocation timeout. Configure the Lambda function to use the SignalResource API operation to signal success or failure to CloudFormation.

questions.explanation:
For an Auto Scaling group update, `cfn-signal` can report the user-data script's success or failure to CloudFormation. Setting `WaitOnResourceSignals` in the Auto Scaling rolling `UpdatePolicy` makes CloudFormation wait for the required successful instance signals. If a failure is signaled or the `PauseTime` timeout expires before the required signals arrive, the stack update fails rather than completing successfully.

**Learn more:** [cfn-signal - AWS CloudFormation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/cfn-signal.html) · [UpdatePolicy attribute - AWS CloudFormation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-attribute-updatepolicy.html)

A company has one developer who writes code for an automated deployment pipeline. The developer stores each project's source code in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company plans to add more developers but is worried about code conflicts and lost work. It also wants to create a test environment to deploy newer code versions for testing, and to let developers automatically deploy to both environments when code changes in the repository.  
  
What is the **MOST** efficient way to satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Create an AWS CodeCommit repository for each project, use the main branch for production code, and create a testing branch for code deployed to testing. Use feature branches to develop new features and pull requests to merge code to testing and main branches.

Create another S3 bucket for each project for testing code, and use an AWS Lambda function to promote code changes between testing and production buckets. Enable versioning on all buckets to prevent code conflicts.

Create an AWS CodeCommit repository for each project, and use the main branch for production and test code with different deployment pipelines for each environment. Use feature branches to develop new features.

Enable versioning and branching on each S3 bucket, use the main branch for production code, and create a testing branch for code deployed to testing. Have developers use each branch for developing in each environment.

questions.explanation:
AWS CodeCommit provides Git repositories with branches and pull requests, enabling developers to work independently on feature branches and merge reviewed changes while managing conflicts. A testing branch and a main production branch support controlled promotion between environments, and CodePipeline can automatically start a pipeline when a commit is made to a configured CodeCommit repository branch.

**Learn more:** [Create a branch in AWS CodeCommit](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/how-to-create-branch.html) · [Create a pull request in AWS CodeCommit](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/how-to-create-pull-request.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses AWS CodePipeline to automate its release pipeline. The pipeline uses AWS CodeDeploy to deploy an application to Amazon ECS with the blue/green deployment model. The company wants to implement scripts that test the green version of the application before traffic is shifted. These scripts will finish in 5 minutes or less. If errors are found during the tests, the application must be rolled back.  
  
Which strategy meets these requirements?

options.text: Add a stage to the CodePipeline pipeline between the source and deploy stages. Use AWS CodeBuild to create an execution environment and build commands in the buildspec file to invoke test scripts. If errors are found, use the aws deploy stop-deployment command to stop the deployment.

Add a stage to the CodePipeline pipeline between the source and deploy stages. Use this stage to execute an AWS Lambda function that will run the test scripts. If errors are found, use the aws deploy stop-deployment command to stop the deployment.

Add a hooks section to the CodeDeploy AppSpec file. Use the AfterAllowTestTraffic lifecycle event to invoke an AWS Lambda function to run the test scripts. If errors are found, exit the Lambda function with an error to trigger rollback.

Add a hooks section to the CodeDeploy AppSpec file. Use the AfterAllowTraffic lifecycle event to invoke the test scripts. If errors are found, use the aws deploy stop-deployment CLI command to stop the deployment.

questions.explanation:
For Amazon ECS blue/green deployments, the CodeDeploy `AfterAllowTestTraffic` AppSpec lifecycle hook runs Lambda validation after test traffic is directed to the replacement task set and before production traffic is shifted. A failed validation result fails the deployment and triggers rollback when rollbacks are configured. A five-minute test fits within Lambda execution limits.

**Learn more:** [AppSpec hooks section for Amazon ECS deployments](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/reference-appspec-file-structure-hooks.html) · [Deployments on the Amazon ECS compute platform](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/deployment-steps-ecs.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A DevOps engineer must create a more stable deployment solution for a web application on AWS. Earlier deployments have caused user-visible bugs, traffic reaching the application too early, and inconsistencies among web servers behind an Application Load Balancer. The current approach stores application code in AWS CodeCommit. When developers push to the repository’s main branch, CodeCommit invokes an AWS Lambda deployment function, which calls an AWS Systems Manager Run Command to build and deploy the new code to every Amazon EC2 instance.  
  
Which combination of actions should be taken to implement a more stable deployment solution? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create a pipeline in AWS CodePipeline with CodeCommit as a source provider. Create parallel pipeline stages to build and test the application. Pass the build artifact to AWS CodeDeploy.
Create a pipeline in AWS CodePipeline with CodeCommit as a source provider. Create separate pipeline stages to build and then test the application. Pass the build artifact to AWS CodeDeploy.
Create and use an AWS CodeDeploy application and deployment group to deploy code updates to the EC2 fleet. Select the Application Load Balancer for the deployment group.
Create individual Lambda functions to run all build, test, and deploy actions using AWS CodeDeploy instead of AWS Systems Manager.
Modify the Lambda function to build a single application package to be shared by all instances. Use AWS CodeDeploy instead of AWS Systems Manager to update the code on the EC2 fleet.

questions.explanation:
AWS CodePipeline stages can enforce a build stage followed by a test stage, passing the resulting artifact to CodeDeploy only through the release workflow. A CodeDeploy EC2/On-Premises deployment group can be associated with a load balancer so instances are removed from serving traffic during an in-place deployment and returned after the deployment succeeds, preventing users from reaching incomplete or inconsistent versions.

**Learn more:** [CodePipeline concepts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/concepts.html) · [Integrating CodeDeploy with Elastic Load Balancing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/integrations-aws-elastic-load-balancing.html)

An IT team has created an AWS CloudFormation template so that others in the company can rapidly and consistently deploy and terminate an application. The template creates an Amazon EC2 instance, including a user data script that installs the application, and an Amazon S3 bucket that the application uses to serve static webpages while it runs.  
  
Every resource must be removed when the CloudFormation stack is deleted. However, the team finds that CloudFormation reports an error during stack deletion and does not delete the S3 bucket created by the stack.  
  
How can the team resolve the error in the **MOST** efficient way while ensuring that all resources are deleted without errors?

options.text: Add a DeletionPolicy attribute to the S3 bucket resource, with the value Delete forcing the bucket to be removed when the stack is deleted.

Add a custom resource with an AWS Lambda function with the DependsOn attribute specifying the S3 bucket, and an IAM role. Write the Lambda function to delete all objects from the bucket when RequestType is Delete.
Identify the resource that was not deleted. From the S3 console, empty the S3 bucket and then delete it.
Replace the EC2 and S3 bucket resources with a single AWS OpsWorks Stacks resource. Define a custom recipe for the stack to create and delete the EC2 instance and the S3 bucket.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 requires a bucket to be empty before it can be deleted. A Lambda-backed CloudFormation custom resource can process the Delete request and remove the bucket’s objects. Declaring that custom resource as dependent on the bucket causes the custom resource to be deleted first, leaving the bucket empty for CloudFormation to delete automatically.

**Learn more:** [AWS::S3::Bucket - AWS CloudFormation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-resource-s3-bucket.html) · [DeletionPolicy attribute - AWS CloudFormation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-attribute-deletionpolicy.html)

",["$","p",null,{"children":["During the investigation, the DevOps engineer finds that the CloudFormation stack status is ",["$","code",null,{"children":"UPDATE_COMPLETE"}],". ",["$","p",null,{"children":"How can the DevOps engineer ensure that the CloudFormation deployment fails if the user data does not successfully complete?"}],"
",["$","$L53",null,{"choices":{"A":"Use the cfn-signal helper script to signal success or failure to CloudFormation. Use the WaitOnResourceSignals update policy within the CloudFormation template. Set an appropriate timeout for the update policy.","B":"Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for the UnhealthyHostCount metric. Include an appropriate alarm threshold for the target group. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic as the target to signal success or failure to CloudFormation.","C":"Create a lifecycle hook on the Auto Scaling group by using the AWS::AutoScaling::LifecycleHook resource. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic as the target to signal success or failure to CloudFormation. Set an appropriate timeout on the lifecycle hook.","D":"Use the Amazon CloudWatch agent to stream the cloud-init logs. Create a subscription filter that includes an AWS Lambda function with an appropriate invocation timeout. Configure the Lambda function to use the SignalResource API operation to signal success or failure to CloudFormation."},"correctAnswer":"A","explanation":"For an Auto Scaling group update, `cfn-signal` can report the user-data script's success or failure to CloudFormation. Setting `WaitOnResourceSignals` in the Auto Scaling rolling `UpdatePolicy` makes CloudFormation wait for the required successful instance signals. If a failure is signaled or the `PauseTime` timeout expires before the required signals arrive, the stack update fails rather than completing successfully.

**Learn more:** [cfn-signal - AWS CloudFormation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/cfn-signal.html) · [UpdatePolicy attribute - AWS CloudFormation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-attribute-updatepolicy.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"c0ca598b-967b-44a7-ac4d-eb51450e8cd2","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-devops-engineer-professional","mode":"default"}}]]
4f:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A company has one developer who writes code for an automated deployment pipeline. The developer stores each project's source code in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company plans to add more developers but is worried about code conflicts and lost work. It also wants to create a test environment to deploy newer code versions for testing, and to let developers automatically deploy to both environments when code changes in the repository."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":["What is the ",["$","strong",null,{"children":"MOST"}]," efficient way to satisfy these requirements?"]}],"
",["$","$L53",null,{"choices":{"A":"Create an AWS CodeCommit repository for each project, use the main branch for production code, and create a testing branch for code deployed to testing. Use feature branches to develop new features and pull requests to merge code to testing and main branches.","B":"Create another S3 bucket for each project for testing code, and use an AWS Lambda function to promote code changes between testing and production buckets. Enable versioning on all buckets to prevent code conflicts.","C":"Create an AWS CodeCommit repository for each project, and use the main branch for production and test code with different deployment pipelines for each environment. Use feature branches to develop new features.","D":"Enable versioning and branching on each S3 bucket, use the main branch for production code, and create a testing branch for code deployed to testing. Have developers use each branch for developing in each environment."},"correctAnswer":"A","explanation":"AWS CodeCommit provides Git repositories with branches and pull requests, enabling developers to work independently on feature branches and merge reviewed changes while managing conflicts. A testing branch and a main production branch support controlled promotion between environments, and CodePipeline can automatically start a pipeline when a commit is made to a configured CodeCommit repository branch.

**Learn more:** [Create a branch in AWS CodeCommit](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/how-to-create-branch.html) · [Create a pull request in AWS CodeCommit](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/how-to-create-pull-request.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"dda29b29-a536-4e3a-bb4e-0aefcec9d3b6","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-devops-engineer-professional","mode":"default"}}]]
50:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A company uses AWS CodePipeline to automate its release pipeline. The pipeline uses AWS CodeDeploy to deploy an application to Amazon ECS with the blue/green deployment model. The company wants to implement scripts that test the green version of the application before traffic is shifted. These scripts will finish in 5 minutes or less. If errors are found during the tests, the application must be rolled back."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"Which strategy meets these requirements?"}],"
",["$","$L53",null,{"choices":{"A":"Add a stage to the CodePipeline pipeline between the source and deploy stages. Use AWS CodeBuild to create an execution environment and build commands in the buildspec file to invoke test scripts. If errors are found, use the aws deploy stop-deployment command to stop the deployment.","B":"Add a stage to the CodePipeline pipeline between the source and deploy stages. Use this stage to execute an AWS Lambda function that will run the test scripts. If errors are found, use the aws deploy stop-deployment command to stop the deployment.","C":"Add a hooks section to the CodeDeploy AppSpec file. Use the AfterAllowTestTraffic lifecycle event to invoke an AWS Lambda function to run the test scripts. If errors are found, exit the Lambda function with an error to trigger rollback.","D":"Add a hooks section to the CodeDeploy AppSpec file. Use the AfterAllowTraffic lifecycle event to invoke the test scripts. If errors are found, use the aws deploy stop-deployment CLI command to stop the deployment."},"correctAnswer":"C","explanation":"For Amazon ECS blue/green deployments, the CodeDeploy `AfterAllowTestTraffic` AppSpec lifecycle hook runs Lambda validation after test traffic is directed to the replacement task set and before production traffic is shifted. A failed validation result fails the deployment and triggers rollback when rollbacks are configured. A five-minute test fits within Lambda execution limits.

**Learn more:** [AppSpec hooks section for Amazon ECS deployments](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/reference-appspec-file-structure-hooks.html) · [Deployments on the Amazon ECS compute platform](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/deployment-steps-ecs.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"f00b0e96-e6b8-4d58-9dea-cd4434c0407e","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-devops-engineer-professional","mode":"default"}}]]
51:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A DevOps engineer must create a more stable deployment solution for a web application on AWS. Earlier deployments have caused user-visible bugs, traffic reaching the application too early, and inconsistencies among web servers behind an Application Load Balancer. The current approach stores application code in AWS CodeCommit. When developers push to the repository’s main branch, CodeCommit invokes an AWS Lambda deployment function, which calls an AWS Systems Manager Run Command to build and deploy the new code to every Amazon EC2 instance."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":["Which combination of actions should be taken to implement a more stable deployment solution?"]}],"
",["$","$L53",null,{"choices":{"A":"Create a pipeline in AWS CodePipeline with CodeCommit as a source provider. Create parallel pipeline stages to build and test the application. Pass the build artifact to AWS CodeDeploy.","B":"Create a pipeline in AWS CodePipeline with CodeCommit as a source provider. Create separate pipeline stages to build and then test the application. Pass the build artifact to AWS CodeDeploy.","C":"Create and use an AWS CodeDeploy application and deployment group to deploy code updates to the EC2 fleet. Select the Application Load Balancer for the deployment group.","D":"Create individual Lambda functions to run all build, test, and deploy actions using AWS CodeDeploy instead of AWS Systems Manager.","E":"Modify the Lambda function to build a single application package to be shared by all instances. Use AWS CodeDeploy instead of AWS Systems Manager to update the code on the EC2 fleet."},"correctAnswer":"BC","explanation":"AWS CodePipeline stages can enforce a build stage followed by a test stage, passing the resulting artifact to CodeDeploy only through the release workflow. A CodeDeploy EC2/On-Premises deployment group can be associated with a load balancer so instances are removed from serving traffic during an in-place deployment and returned after the deployment succeeds, preventing users from reaching incomplete or inconsistent versions.

A security team is worried that a developer could accidentally associate an Elastic IP address with an Amazon EC2 instance in production. Developers must not be permitted to associate an Elastic IP address with an instance. The security team must receive notification whenever any production server has an Elastic IP address at any time.  
  
How can this be automated?

options.text: Use Amazon Athena to query AWS CloudTrail logs to check for any associate-address attempts. Create an AWS Lambda function to disassociate the Elastic IP address from the instance, and alert the security team.

Attach an IAM policy to the developers' IAM group to deny associate-address permissions. Create a custom AWS Config rule to check whether an Elastic IP address is associated with any instance tagged as production, and alert the security team.

Ensure that all IAM groups associated with developers do not have associate-address permissions. Create a scheduled AWS Lambda function to check whether an Elastic IP address is associated with any instance tagged as production, and alert the security team if an instance has an Elastic IP address associated with it.

Create an AWS Config rule to check that all production instances have EC2 IAM roles that include deny associate-address permissions. Verify whether there is an Elastic IP address associated with any instance, and alert the security team if an instance has an Elastic IP address associated with it.

questions.explanation:
An identity-based IAM policy with an explicit `Deny` for `ec2:AssociateAddress` overrides any matching allow granted to members of the developers’ IAM group, preventing them from associating Elastic IP addresses. A custom AWS Config rule can evaluate production-tagged EC2 instances when configuration changes occur, identify an Elastic IP association as noncompliant, and send a compliance notification to the security team.

**Learn more:** [IAM explicit deny precedence](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_examples_ec2_terminate-ip.html) · [Creating AWS Config Custom Lambda Rules](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/evaluate-config_develop-rules_lambda-functions.html)

A company has a VPC that contains a public subnet and a private subnet. The company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances in the private subnet. An Application Load Balancer in the public subnet distributes traffic to the EC2 instances.  
  
The company has enabled Amazon GuardDuty for the account. Its DevOps team maintains a list of external IP ranges that is updated daily. The list is stored in an Amazon S3 bucket in the account. A DevOps engineer must configure GuardDuty to create a GuardDuty finding when traffic to the application originates from an IP range in the external IP range list.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs daily and invokes an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to retrieve the most recent list of external IP ranges from the S3 bucket. For each IP range in the list, configure the Lambda function to create a GuardDuty finding filter on the publicIp filter attribute.

Configure a threat list in GuardDuty. Set the source as the list of external IP ranges in the S3 bucket. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs daily and invokes an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to refresh the threat list in GuardDuty to match the list of external IP ranges in the S3 bucket.

Configure a trusted IP list in GuardDuty. Set the source as the list of external IP ranges in the S3 bucket. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs daily and invokes an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to refresh the trusted IP list in GuardDuty to match the list of external IP ranges in the S3 bucket.

Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs daily and invokes an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to retrieve the most recent list of external IP ranges from the S3 bucket. For each IP range in the list, configure the Lambda function to create a GuardDuty finding filter on the localIp filter attribute.

questions.explanation:
A GuardDuty threat IP list uses IP addresses or CIDR ranges identified as malicious sources to generate findings when GuardDuty detects activity involving them. The list can be sourced from Amazon S3 and must be refreshed after its S3 contents change. A daily EventBridge-triggered Lambda function can refresh the threat list to reflect the daily S3 update. Trusted IP lists suppress findings, and GuardDuty finding filters do not create new findings.

**Learn more:** [Customizing threat detection with entity lists and IP address lists](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/guardduty_upload-lists.html) · [Updating an entity list or IP address list](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/guardduty-lists-update-procedure.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company’s DevOps engineer administers an organization in AWS Organizations. The organization contains many accounts. The company requires all AWS CloudFormation stacks in production accounts to have termination protection enabled. Termination protection is not required for non-production accounts.  
  
The company has assigned a centralized account for AWS Config aggregation and has configured every account to support AWS CloudFormation and AWS Config. The company has also placed all production accounts into an OU.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an AWS Config rule to detect stacks that do not have termination protection enabled. Add a remediation action to the rule to enable termination protection. Deploy the rule across the organization by using the PutOrganizationConfigRule API operation.

Create a CloudFormation template that deploys an AWS Config rule to detect stacks that do not have termination protection enabled. Add a remediation action to the rule to enable termination protection. Deploy the template to the OU of the production accounts by using CloudFormation StackSets.
Create an SCP that denies cloudformation:DeleteStack actions. Apply the SCP to the OU of the production accounts by using CloudFormation StackSets.
Create a CloudFormation stack policy that denies Update:Delete actions. Apply the policy to the OU of the production accounts by using CloudFormation StackSets.

questions.explanation:
The AWS Config managed rule `CLOUDFORMATION_TERMINATION_PROTECTION_CHECK` marks a CloudFormation stack noncompliant when termination protection is not enabled. Deploying that rule and its remediation configuration through CloudFormation StackSets to the production OU limits both detection and automatic remediation to production accounts. A company uses AWS Organizations to administer its AWS accounts. A DevOps engineer wants to deploy a new AWS Lambda function to every account in the organization by using AWS CloudFormation StackSets. The DevOps engineer uses a delegated administrator account to deploy the stack sets to member accounts. The stack operation continues to fail, and the stack instance status is `OUTDATED`.  
  
Which actions should the DevOps engineer take to resolve this error? (Choose two.)

options.text: Ensure that the AWS Region is the same for the stack sets and the target resources.
Ensure that the delegated administrator account has a trust relationship with the target account.
Ensure that the resources in the stacks do not have termination protection enabled by default.
Ensure that the CloudFormation template is creating unique global resources.
Deploy the stack sets from the management account and not from the delegated administrator account.

questions.explanation:
An `OUTDATED` StackSet instance can result when the administrator account lacks a trust relationship with a target account. It can also result when the template attempts to create global resources, such as Amazon S3 buckets or IAM roles, whose names conflict and therefore are not unique. Delegated administrator accounts are supported for service-managed StackSets.

**Learn more:** [Troubleshooting CloudFormation StackSets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/stacksets-troubleshooting.html) · [Best practices for using CloudFormation StackSets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/stacksets-bestpractices.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A development team uses AWS CodeCommit, AWS CodePipeline, and AWS CodeBuild to develop and deploy an application. Over time, the number of pull requests has grown. The pipeline is frequently blocked by failed tests. To avoid this blockage, the development team wants to run unit and integration tests for every pull request before it is merged.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a CodeBuild project to run the unit and integration tests. Create a CodeCommit approval rule template. Configure the template to require the successful invocation of the CodeBuild project. Attach the approval rule to the project's CodeCommit repository.

Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule to match pullRequestCreated events from CodeCommit. Create a CodeBuild project to run the unit and integration tests. Configure the CodeBuild project as a target of the EventBridge (CloudWatch Events) rule that includes a custom event payload with the CodeCommit repository and branch information from the event.

Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule to match pullRequestCreated events from CodeCommit. Modify the existing CodePipeline pipeline to not run the deploy steps if the build is started from a pull request. Configure the EventBridge (CloudWatch Events) rule to run the pipeline with a custom payload that contains the CodeCommit repository and branch information from the event.

Create a CodeBuild project to run the unit and integration tests. Create a CodeCommit notification rule that matches when a pull request is created or updated. Configure the notification rule to invoke the CodeBuild project.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EventBridge receives AWS CodeCommit pull-request events and can invoke AWS CodeBuild as a rule target. Matching pull-request creation and passing the repository and branch information to a dedicated CodeBuild project runs unit and integration tests before the pull request is merged, preventing failing pull requests from blocking the post-merge pipeline.

**Learn more:** [AWS CodeCommit events - Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/ref/events-ref-codecommit.html) · [Event bus targets in Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-targets.html)

A media company operates several thousand Amazon EC2 instances in an AWS account. The company uses Slack and a shared email inbox for team communication and important updates. A DevOps engineer must send every AWS-scheduled EC2 maintenance notification to the Slack channel and the shared inbox. The solution must include each instance’s **Name** and **Owner** tags.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Integrate AWS Trusted Advisor with AWS Config. Configure a custom AWS Config rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function to publish notifications to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe a Slack channel endpoint and the shared inbox to the topic.

Use Amazon EventBridge to monitor for AWS Health events. Configure the maintenance events to target an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe an AWS Lambda function to the SNS topic to send notifications to the Slack channel and the shared inbox.

Create an AWS Lambda function that sends EC2 maintenance notifications to the Slack channel and the shared inbox. Monitor EC2 health events by using Amazon CloudWatch metrics. Configure a CloudWatch alarm that invokes the Lambda function when a maintenance notification is received.

Configure AWS Support integration with AWS CloudTrail. Create a CloudTrail lookup event to invoke an AWS Lambda function to pass EC2 maintenance notifications to Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS). Configure Amazon SNS to target the Slack channel and the shared inbox.

questions.explanation:
AWS Health sends scheduled EC2 maintenance notifications as account-specific events that Amazon EventBridge can monitor. The Health event identifies the affected instances, and a Lambda function can retrieve their EC2 Name and Owner tags before sending formatted messages to Slack and the shared inbox. Amazon SNS provides the fan-out path to invoke the Lambda function for the notifications. AWS Config, CloudWatch metrics, Trusted Advisor, and CloudTrail lookup events are not the appropriate source for AWS-scheduled EC2 maintenance events.

**Learn more:** [Monitoring events in AWS Health with Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/health/latest/ug/cloudwatch-events-health.html) · [AWS Health events Amazon EventBridge schema](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/health/latest/ug/aws-health-events-eventbridge-schema.html)

A DevOps team uses AWS CloudFormation to create its infrastructure. The security team is concerned that sensitive parameters, such as passwords, could be exposed.  
  
Which combination of steps will improve AWS CloudFormation security? (Choose three.)

options.text: Create a secure string with AWS KMS and choose a KMS encryption key. Reference the ARN of the secure string, and give AWS CloudFormation permission to the KMS key for decryption.

Create secrets using the AWS Secrets Manager AWS::SecretsManager::Secret resource type. Reference the secret resource return attributes in resources that need a password, such as an Amazon RDS database.
Store sensitive static data as secure strings in the AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Use dynamic references in the resources that need access to the data.
Store sensitive static data in the AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store as strings. Reference the stored value using types of Systems Manager parameters.
Use AWS KMS to encrypt the CloudFormation template.
Use the CloudFormation NoEcho parameter property to mask the parameter value.

questions.explanation:
AWS CloudFormation security guidance recommends storing passwords and other secrets in AWS Secrets Manager or as Systems Manager Parameter Store SecureString parameters, rather than embedding them in templates. Secrets are consumed securely through dynamic references, and SecureString parameters use the `ssm-secure` dynamic-reference pattern. Setting a sensitive CloudFormation parameter’s `NoEcho` property to `true` masks its value in stack descriptions, console output, CLI output, and API responses, although it is not a substitute for external secret storage.

**Learn more:** [AWS CloudFormation best practices](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/best-practices.html) · [Get a secure string value from Systems Manager Parameter Store](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/dynamic-references-ssm-secure-strings.html)

What should the DevOps engineer do to achieve this in the **MOST** maintainable way?

options.text: Automate patching and upgrading using AWS Systems Manager on EC2 instances and encrypt Amazon EBS volumes by default.
Deploy Jenkins to an Amazon ECS cluster and copy build artifacts to an Amazon S3 bucket with default encryption enabled.
Leverage AWS CodePipeline with a build action and encrypt the artifacts using AWS Secrets Manager.
Use AWS CodeBuild with artifact encryption to replace the Jenkins instance running on Amazon EC2.

questions.explanation:
AWS CodeBuild is a fully managed build service that eliminates the need to provision, patch, update, and manage build servers. It produces build artifacts and supports encryption of build output artifacts with AWS KMS, satisfying both the operational-maintenance and intellectual-property protection requirements.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates a web application that users reach over the internet. The web application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The EC2 instances are in an Auto Scaling group. The ALB is associated with a security group that permits traffic from the internet. The web application maintains a local cache on each EC2 instance.  
  
During a recent security incident, requests overloaded the web application and caused an outage for the company's customers. In response, the company placed Amazon CloudFront in front of the web application. All customers now reach the web application through CloudFront.  
  
A DevOps engineer must implement a solution that routes every request through CloudFront. The solution must also provide the company with the ability to block requests according to request content, such as header or body information.  
  
Which combination of steps should the DevOps engineer take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create an AWS WAF web ACL. Associate the web ACL with the CloudFront distribution. Create rules for each type of traffic that the company wants to block.

Create new ALB listener rules on the existing listeners. Configure the new rules to allow or reject incoming traffic based on whether the host header matches the CloudFront fully qualified domain name (FQDN).

Create an AWS PrivateLink endpoint service for the ALB Configure the endpoint service to allow requests from CloudFront. Update the web application origin in CloudFront to use the newly created endpoint service's DNS name.

Create a CloudFront origin access identity (OAI) for the web application. Update the web application origin in CloudFront to use the OAI Update the ALB rules to check for the OAI and return an HTTP 403 error if the OAI header is not present.

Create an AWS Firewall Manager security policy. Attach the security policy to the CloudFront distribution. Use the security policy to attach AWS WAF rule groups for each type of traffic that the company wants to block.

questions.explanation:
To block requests by their content (headers or body), the correct tool is AWS WAF: create a web ACL, associate it with the CloudFront distribution, and add rules for the traffic to block (option A). To guarantee that every request actually passes through CloudFront rather than hitting the ALB directly, add ALB listener rules that allow or reject traffic based on whether the Host header matches the CloudFront FQDN (option B) — direct-to-ALB requests carry a different host value and are rejected. Option D is wrong because CloudFront origin access identity works only with Amazon S3 origins, not an ALB. Option C (PrivateLink endpoint service as a CloudFront origin) is not a supported/standard pattern for this goal, and option E (Firewall Manager) is an unnecessary, higher-overhead duplicate of the WAF web ACL in option A.

**Learn more:** [Restrict ALB traffic to only CloudFront](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/waf-restrict-alb-allow-cloudfront) · [Enhance CloudFront origin security with AWS WAF](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/how-to-enhance-amazon-cloudfront-origin-security-with-aws-waf-and-aws-secrets-manager/)

A company intends to discontinue use of Amazon EC2 key pairs for SSH access and instead use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager. To further improve security, Session Manager access must occur only over a private network.  
  
Which combinations of actions will achieve this? (Choose two.)

options.text: Allow inbound access to TCP port 22 in all associated EC2 security groups from the VPC CIDR range.
Attach an IAM policy with the necessary Systems Manager permissions to the existing IAM instance profile.
Create a VPC endpoint for Systems Manager in the desired Region.
Deploy a new EC2 instance that will act as a bastion host to the rest of the EC2 instance fleet.
Remove any default routes in the associated route tables.

questions.explanation:
An EC2 instance must have an IAM instance profile that grants the required Systems Manager permissions in order to be managed and accessed with Session Manager. An AWS Systems Manager interface VPC endpoint, using AWS PrivateLink, enables private IP connectivity and keeps traffic between managed nodes, Systems Manager, and Amazon EC2 on the Amazon network without requiring internet access.

**Learn more:** [Improve the security of EC2 instances by using VPC endpoints for Systems Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/setup-create-vpc.html) · [Use AWS PrivateLink to set up a VPC endpoint for Session Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/session-manager-getting-started-privatelink.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A healthcare services company is concerned about rising software-licensing costs for an application that monitors patient wellness. The company wants to establish an audit process to confirm that the application runs only on Amazon EC2 Dedicated Hosts. A DevOps Engineer must create a workflow to audit the application for compliance.  
  
Which steps should the Engineer take to satisfy this requirement with the **LEAST** administrative overhead?

options.text: Use AWS Systems Manager Configuration Compliance. Use calls to the put-compliance-items API action to scan and build a database of noncompliant EC2 instances based on their host placement configuration. Use an Amazon DynamoDB table to store these instance IDs for fast access. Generate a report through Systems Manager by calling the list-compliance-summaries API action.

Use custom Java code running on an EC2 instance. Set up EC2 Auto Scaling for the instance depending on the number of instances to be checked. Send the list of noncompliant EC2 instance IDs to an Amazon SQS queue. Set up another worker instance to process instance IDs from the SQS queue and write them to Amazon DynamoDB. Use an AWS Lambda function to terminate noncompliant instance IDs obtained from the queue, and send them to an Amazon SNS email topic for distribution.

Use AWS Config. Identify all EC2 instances to be audited by enabling Config Recording on all Amazon EC2 resources for the region. Create a custom AWS Config rule that triggers an AWS Lambda function by using the ג€config-rule-change-triggeredג€ blueprint. Modify the Lambda evaluateCompliance() function to verify host placement to return a NON_COMPLIANT result if the instance is not running on an EC2 Dedicated Host. Use the AWS Config report to address noncompliant instances.

Use AWS CloudTrail. Identify all EC2 instances to be audited by analyzing all calls to the EC2 RunCommand API action. Invoke an AWS Lambda function that analyzes the host placement of the instance. Store the EC2 instance ID of noncompliant resources in an Amazon RDS MySQL DB instance. Generate a report by querying the RDS instance and exporting the query results to a CSV text file.

questions.explanation:
AWS Config records EC2 resource configurations and evaluates them against compliance rules. A custom Lambda-backed AWS Config rule can be scoped to EC2 instances, evaluate their Dedicated Host placement when configuration changes occur, return `NON_COMPLIANT` for instances that are not on Dedicated Hosts, and provide compliance reporting without operating separate databases, queues, or worker instances.

**Learn more:** [Creating AWS Config Custom Lambda Rules](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/evaluate-config_develop-rules_lambda-functions.html) · [Adding AWS Config Rules](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/evaluate-config_add-rules.html)

An AWS CodePipeline pipeline implements a code-release process. The pipeline integrates with AWS CodeDeploy to deploy application versions to multiple Amazon EC2 instances at each CodePipeline stage.  
  
A recent deployment failed because of a CodeDeploy issue. The DevOps team wants to enhance deployment monitoring and notifications to reduce resolution times.  
  
What should the DevOps Engineer do to generate notifications when issues are detected?

options.text: Implement AWS CloudWatch Logs for CodePipeline and CodeDeploy, create an AWS Config rule to evaluate code deployment issues, and create an Amazon SNS topic to notify stakeholders of deployment issues.

Implement AWS CloudWatch Events for CodePipeline and CodeDeploy, create an AWS Lambda function to evaluate code deployment issues, and create an Amazon SNS topic to notify stakeholders of deployment issues.

Implement AWS CloudTrail to record CodePipeline and CodeDeploy API call information, create an AWS Lambda function to evaluate code deployment issues, and create an Amazon SNS topic to notify stakeholders of deployment issues.

Implement AWS CloudWatch Events for CodePipeline and CodeDeploy, create an Amazon Inspector assessment target to evaluate code deployment issues, and create an Amazon SNS topic to notify stakeholders of deployment issues.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EventBridge (formerly Amazon CloudWatch Events) receives CodePipeline and CodeDeploy state-change events. EventBridge rules can invoke an AWS Lambda function to evaluate deployment-failure details, and Lambda can publish notifications to an Amazon SNS topic for stakeholders. AWS Config, CloudTrail, and Amazon Inspector do not provide the appropriate event-driven deployment-failure evaluation flow.

**Learn more:** [AWS CodePipeline: Monitor events](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/detect-state-changes-cloudwatch-events.html) · [AWS CodeDeploy: Create a trigger for a CodeDeploy event](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/monitoring-sns-event-notifications-create-trigger.html)
