lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A large company has acquired a small company. The large company has an AWS Organizations organization. It must integrate the small company’s single AWS account into that organization with minimal effect on the applications deployed in the small company's account.  
  
The large company has deployed AWS Control Tower in its organization and wants to enroll the small company’s account in AWS Control Tower. The large company’s AWS Control Tower configuration includes a security OU, a sandbox OU, and a new destination OU set up for the small company's migration. Each company uses AWS Config as part of its account management strategy.  
  
Which combination of steps should a DevOps engineer take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create a landing zone in the security OU of the large company's AWS Control Tower landing zone. Provide the account's email address, the account owners first and last name, and the name of the landing zone created in the security OU to complete the AWS Control Tower Account Factory enrollment request.

Create and apply SCPs in the destination OU to restrict the types of resources that can be created in the small company’s account. Assess the impact of the applied SCPs on the small company's account. Delete existing SCPs in the small company’s account.

Create an AWS Config conformance pack that contains the policies that are currently applied to the large company's account. Use AWS Config to assess the impact that enrollment in AWS Control Tower will have on the small company's account. Delete the configuration recorder and delivery channels from the AWS Config settings of the small company's account.

Enroll the OU of the small company's account in the large company’s AWS Control Tower environment. Specify the destination OU in the large company's AWS Control Tower landing zone as the receiving OU in the request.

Create an AWSControlTowerExecution role in the small company's account. Provide the account's email address, the account owner's first and last name, and the destination OU to complete the AWS Control Tower Account Factory enrollment request.

questions.explanation:
Existing accounts must have the AWSControlTowerExecution role so AWS Control Tower can establish the required trusted access and deploy its governance baselines. Existing AWS Config configuration recorders and delivery channels can conflict with AWS Control Tower’s AWS Config baseline and must be removed or appropriately modified before enrollment. An AWS Config conformance pack can assess the impact of applicable Control Tower controls before the migration.

**Learn more:** [Prerequisites for enrollment - AWS Control Tower](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/userguide/enrollment-prerequisites.html) · [Enroll an existing account from the AWS Control Tower console](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/userguide/quick-account-provisioning.html)

A company runs its staging website on an Amazon EC2 instance backed by Amazon EBS storage. The company needs rapid recovery with minimal data loss if the EC2 instance experiences network connectivity problems or power failures.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Add the instance to an EC2 Auto Scaling group with the minimum, maximum, and desired capacity set to 1.
Add the instance to an EC2 Auto Scaling group with a lifecycle hook to detach the EBS volume when the EC2 instance shuts down or terminates.
Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for the StatusCheckFailed_System metric and select the EC2 action to recover the instance.
Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for the StatusCheckFailed_Instance metric and select the EC2 action to reboot the instance.

questions.explanation:
EC2 system status-check failures cover underlying host problems such as loss of network connectivity or system power. A CloudWatch alarm using `StatusCheckFailed_System` can trigger EC2 instance recovery, which moves the instance to healthy hardware while retaining its attached EBS volumes. Recovery actions cannot be used with `StatusCheckFailed_Instance`.

**Learn more:** [Configure CloudWatch action based recovery on an EC2 instance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/cloudwatch-recovery.html) · [Automatic instance recovery](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-instance-recover.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company’s primary AWS Region has the following infrastructure:  
  
- An Amazon S3 bucket containing an object package that instance user data uses to configure an application.  
- Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB), using an instance profile that grants `s3:Get*` access to the S3 bucket.  
  
The company has the following infrastructure in a backup Region:  
  
- An S3 bucket with the same configuration as the S3 bucket in the primary AWS Region, but with no objects.  
- EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an ALB that use the same configuration as in the primary AWS Region.  
  
To simulate a disaster-recovery scenario, the company disables all Amazon S3 access and sets the Auto Scaling group’s minimum, maximum, and desired instance counts to 0 in the primary Region. When instances in the backup Region scale out, they fail Amazon Route 53 health checks.  
  
Which combination of steps should the company take to fix this issue? (Choose three.)

options.text: Update the Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling service-linked role to allow access to both S3 buckets.
Set up S3 Cross-Region Replication from the S3 bucket in the primary Region to the S3 bucket in the backup Region.
Update the instance user data to reference the S3 bucket in the primary Region.
Increase the timeout for the target group health check.
Update the EC2 instance profile to allow s3:list* actions.
Update the EC2 instance profile to allow read access to both S3 buckets.

questions.explanation:
S3 Cross-Region Replication copies the application package to the bucket in the backup Region so that the recovery environment has the required object. The EC2 instance profile needs read access to both buckets so instances can retrieve the package from either permitted location. Target-group health checks fail when a target does not respond within the configured timeout; increasing that timeout accommodates application startup and package retrieval before the target responds successfully.

**Learn more:** [Replicating objects within and across Regions - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication.html) · [Troubleshoot your Application Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-troubleshooting.html)

A company runs microservices in AWS Lambda that read data from Amazon DynamoDB. Developers manually deploy the Lambda code after tests succeed. The company now requires the tests and deployments to be automated and to run in the cloud. In addition, traffic to each microservice's new version must be gradually shifted over time after deployment.  
  
Which solution meets all requirements while providing the **MOST** developer velocity?

options.text: Create an AWS CodePipeline configuration and set up a post-commit hook to trigger the pipeline after tests have passed. Use AWS CodeDeploy and create a Canary deployment configuration that specifies the percentage of traffic and interval.

Create an AWS CodeBuild configuration that triggers when the test code is pushed. Use AWS CloudFormation to trigger an AWS CodePipeline configuration that deploys the new Lambda versions and specifies the traffic shift percentage and interval.

Create an AWS CodePipeline configuration and set up the source code step to trigger when code is pushed. Set up the build step to use AWS CodeBuild to run the tests. Set up an AWS CodeDeploy configuration to deploy, then select the CodeDeployDefault.LambdaLinea10PercentEvery3Minutes option.

Use the AWS CLI to set up a post-commit hook that uploads the code to an Amazon S3 bucket after tests have passed. Set up an S3 event trigger that runs a Lambda function that deploys the new version. Use an interval in the Lambda function to deploy the code over time at the required percentage.

questions.explanation:
AWS CodePipeline can be triggered by source-code changes and orchestrate a build stage that uses AWS CodeBuild for automated tests, followed by AWS CodeDeploy for Lambda deployment. The `CodeDeployDefault.LambdaLinear10PercentEvery3Minutes` deployment configuration shifts 10% of traffic to the new Lambda version every three minutes until all traffic is shifted, meeting the requirement for incremental traffic shifting over time.

**Learn more:** [Working with deployment configurations in CodeDeploy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/deployment-configurations.html) · [Tutorial: Lambda function deployments with CodePipeline](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/tutorials-lambda-deploy.html)

A company uses AWS CodePipeline to deploy an application. Under a new guideline, a member of the company’s security team must approve every application change before it is deployed to production. The approval must be logged and retained.  
  
Which combination of actions meets these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Configure CodePipeline to write actions to Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
Configure CodePipeline to write actions to an Amazon S3 bucket at the end of each pipeline stage.
Create an AWS CloudTrail trail to deliver logs to Amazon S3.
Create a CodePipeline custom action to invoke an AWS Lambda function for approval. Create a policy that gives the security team access to manage CodePipeline custom actions.
Create a CodePipeline manual approval action before the deployment step. Create a policy that grants the security team access to approve manual approval stages.

questions.explanation:
A CodePipeline manual approval action placed before production deployment pauses the pipeline until an IAM-authorized security-team member submits an approval or rejection through `codepipeline:PutApprovalResult`. CloudTrail records AWS API activity with identity and request details, and a trail delivers those records continuously to an Amazon S3 bucket for durable retention.

**Learn more:** [Add a manual approval action to a stage - AWS CodePipeline](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/approvals.html) · [Grant approval permissions to an IAM user in CodePipeline](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/approvals-iam-permissions.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company deployed an application on AWS Elastic Beanstalk using an all-at-once deployment method. A recent deployment failed because of an application misconfiguration, causing significant downtime.  
  
To avoid this downtime in the future while maintaining application performance, a DevOps engineer must revise the deployment method. The engineer must ensure that application versions are configured consistently across every instance without creating new environments.  
  
Which deployment solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Switch to a rolling deployment strategy for future application updates.
Switch to a rolling deployment with additional batch strategy for future application updates.
Switch to an immutable deployment strategy for future application updates.
Switch to a blue/green deployment strategy for future application updates.

questions.explanation:
An immutable deployment launches a new, temporary Auto Scaling group of instances running the new application version while the existing instances continue to serve traffic. If the deployment or health checks fail, Elastic Beanstalk terminates the new group and keeps the original fleet intact, preventing a partially updated fleet and associated downtime. This deployment occurs within the existing Elastic Beanstalk environment.

**Learn more:** [AWS Elastic Beanstalk deployment policies and settings](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/using-features.rolling-version-deploy.html) · [AWS Elastic Beanstalk immutable environment updates](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/environmentmgmt-updates-immutable.html)

options.text: Create a new AWS CodeBuild project. Configure the user name and password in an environment variable. Use the user name and password to run the command-line integration steps. Update the CodePipeline pipeline to include a new scan stage. In the new scan stage, include a test action that uses the newly created CodeBuild project.

Create a new AWS CodeBuild project. Store the user name and password as a secret in AWS Secrets Manager Read the secret from Secrets Manager. Use the user name and password to run the command-line integration steps. Update the CodePipeline pipeline to include a new scan stage. In the new scan stage, include a test action that uses the newly created CodeBuild project.

Create a new AWS CodeBuild project. Store the user name and password as a string in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Read the string from Parameter Store. Use the user name and password to run the command-line integration steps. Update the CodePipeline pipeline to include a new scan stage. In the new scan stage, include a test action that uses the newly created CodeBuild project.

Upload the user name and password in an encrypted JSON file to an Amazon S3 bucket that has a specific policy to allow only administrators to read the file. Create a new AWS CodeBuild project. Use the user name and password from the file in Amazon S3 to run the command-line integration steps. Update the CodePipeline pipeline to include a new scan stage. In the new scan stage, include a test action that uses the newly created CodeBuild project.

questions.explanation:
AWS Secrets Manager is purpose-built to store and retrieve application credentials securely: secrets are encrypted at rest, retrieved over TLS, access can be restricted with IAM, and credentials can be rotated. A CodeBuild project can retrieve the secret at runtime to execute the third-party scan, and a failing CodeBuild test action stops CodePipeline from progressing to deployment.

**Learn more:** [AWS Secrets Manager best practices](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/best-practices.html) · [AWS CodeBuild build specification reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/build-spec-ref.html)

A DevOps team supports numerous accounts throughout an organization in AWS Organizations. The DevOps team has chosen to use AWS Coring throughout the organization to implement centralized, automatic remediation for Amazon S3 buckets with public ACLs. Individual accounts must be unable to change the remediation strategy.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an AWS Config conformance pack that contains a rule that checks for S3 buckets that have public ACLs. Configure the conformance pack to use an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook to block public access to the S3 buckets. Deploy the conformance pack across the organization.

Configure AWS Config rules that detect S3 buckets that have public ACLs. Configure a remediation action that uses AWS Lambda to block public access to the S3 buckets. Use AWS CloudFormation StackSets to deploy the rules across the organization.

Configure AWS Config rules that detect S3 buckets that have public ACLs. Configure a remediation action that uses an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook to block public access to the S3 buckets. Use AWS CloudFormation StackSets to deploy the rules across the organization.

Create an AWS Config conformance pack that contains a rule that checks for 53 buckets that have public ACLs. Configure the conformance pack to use an AWS Lambda function to block public access to the S3 buckets. Deploy the conformance pack across the organization.

questions.explanation:
An AWS Config organization conformance pack packages compliance rules and Systems Manager Automation remediation actions for centralized deployment across AWS Organizations. The management account can ensure that member accounts cannot modify the underlying AWS Config rules and remediation actions. AWS Config performs remediation through AWS Systems Manager Automation documents, making this the supported automated-remediation mechanism.

**Learn more:** [Managing Conformance Packs for AWS Config Across All Accounts in Your Organization](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/conformance-pack-organization-apis.html) · [Remediating Noncompliant Resources with AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/remediation.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company deploys its multi-Region applications by using a series of separate Amazon CloudFormation templates. The templates have to be deployed in a particular order. The company is making more changes to the templates than it had anticipated and wants to deploy new templates more efficiently. In addition, the data engineering team must receive notification of every template change.  
  
What should the company do to meet these goals?

options.text: Create an AWS Lambda function to deploy the CloudFormation templates in the required order. Use stack policies to alert the data engineering team.
Host the CloudFormation templates in Amazon S3. Use Amazon S3 events to directly trigger CloudFormation updates and Amazon SNS notifications.
Implement CloudFormation StackSets and use drift detection to trigger update alerts to the data engineering team.
Leverage CloudFormation nested stacks and stack sets for deployments. Use Amazon SNS to notify the data engineering team.

questions.explanation:
CloudFormation nested stacks organize separate templates under a parent stack, enabling dependent components to be deployed and updated as one hierarchy. CloudFormation StackSets provision stacks across AWS Regions and can perform sequential deployments in a specified Region order. Amazon SNS notification ARNs can notify the data engineering team about stack operations.

**Learn more:** [Split a template into reusable pieces using nested stacks](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/using-cfn-nested-stacks.html) · [StackSets concepts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/stacksets-concepts.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an on-premises application written in Go. A DevOps engineer must migrate the application to AWS. The company’s development team wants to enable blue/green deployments and carry out A/B testing.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Deploy the application on an Amazon EC2 instance and create an AMI of this instance. Use this AMI to create an automatic scaling launch configuration that is used in an Auto Scaling group. Use an Elastic Load Balancer to distribute traffic. When changes are made to the application, a new AMI will be created, which will initiate an EC2 instance refresh.

Use Amazon Lightsail to deploy the application. Store the application in a zipped format in an Amazon S3 bucket. Use this zipped version to deploy new versions of the application to Lightsail. Use Lightsail deployment options to manage the deployment.

Use AWS CodeArtifact to store the application code. Use AWS CodeDeploy to deploy the application to a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. Use Elastic Load Balancing to distribute the traffic to the EC2 instances. When making changes to the application, upload a new version to CodeArtifact and create a new CodeDeploy deployment.

Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk to host the application. Store a zipped version of the application in Amazon S3, and use that location to deploy new versions of the application using Elastic Beanstalk to manage the deployment options.

questions.explanation:
AWS Elastic Beanstalk supports Go applications deployed as source bundles from Amazon S3. It supports blue/green deployments through separate environments and environment-URL swaps, and its traffic-splitting deployment policy directs a defined percentage of incoming traffic to a new application version for an evaluation period. This provides the controlled traffic exposure needed for A/B-style testing.

**Learn more:** [Blue/Green deployments with Elastic Beanstalk](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/using-features.CNAMESwap.html) · [Elastic Beanstalk deployment policies and settings](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/using-features.rolling-version-deploy.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has numerous applications. Different teams developed the applications using multiple languages and frameworks. The applications run both on premises and across different servers with different operating systems. Each team uses its own release protocol and process. The company wants to reduce the complexity involved in releasing and maintaining these applications.  
  
The company is migrating its technology stacks, including these applications, to AWS. It wants centralized source-code control, a consistent automated delivery pipeline, and as few underlying-infrastructure maintenance tasks as possible.  
  
What should a DevOps engineer do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Create one AWS CodeCommit repository for all applications. Put each application's code in different branch. Merge the branches, and use AWS CodeBuild to build the applications. Use AWS CodeDeploy to deploy the applications to one centralized application server.

Create one AWS CodeCommit repository for each of the applications Use AWS CodeBuild to build the applications one at a time. Use AWS CodeDeploy to deploy the applications to one centralized application server.

Create one AWS CodeCommit repository for each of the applications. Use AWS CodeBuild to build the applications one at a time to create one AMI for each server. Use AWS CloudFormation StackSets to automatically provision and decommission Amazon EC2 fleets by using these AMIs.

Create one AWS CodeCommit repository for each of the applications. Use AWS CodeBuild to build one Docker image for each application in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). Use AWS CodeDeploy to deploy the applications to Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on infrastructure that AWS Fargate manages.

questions.explanation:
Per-application repositories preserve centralized source control while isolating independently developed applications. Building each application into a Docker image, storing it in Amazon ECR, and deploying it to Amazon ECS standardizes delivery across languages and operating systems. AWS Fargate is serverless container compute, so AWS manages the underlying infrastructure, minimizing server maintenance; CodeDeploy supports deployments to Amazon ECS.

**Learn more:** [What is AWS Fargate?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/AWS_Fargate.html) · [What is CodeDeploy?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/welcome.html)

A company has several child accounts that belong to an organization in AWS Organizations. The security team must review every Amazon EC2 security group and its inbound and outbound rules. The team wants to retrieve this information programmatically from the child accounts by using an AWS Lambda function in the organization's management account.  
  
Which combination of access changes will satisfy these requirements? (Choose three.)

options.text: Create a trust relationship that allows users in the child accounts to assume the management account IAM role.
Create a trust relationship that allows users in the management account to assume the IAM roles of the child accounts.
Create an IAM role in each child account that has access to the AmazonEC2ReadOnlyAccess managed policy.
Create an IAM role in each child account to allow the sts:AssumeRole action against the management account IAM role's ARN.
Create an IAM role in the management account that allows the sts:AssumeRole action against the child account IAM role's ARN.
Create an IAM role in the management account that has access to the AmazonEC2ReadOnlyAccess managed policy.

questions.explanation:
Cross-account role access requires a role in each child account whose trust policy permits the management-account principal to assume it, and an identity policy on that management-account principal that permits `sts:AssumeRole` on the child roles. The assumed child-account role needs EC2 read-only permissions to retrieve security groups and their rules; `AmazonEC2ReadOnlyAccess` provides read-only access to Amazon EC2.

**Learn more:** [IAM roles — AWS Identity and Access Management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles.html) · [Grant a user permissions to switch roles — AWS IAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_use_permissions-to-switch.html)

A company modified the AWS CloudFormation template for a critical business application. The stack update failed because of an error in the revised template, and AWS CloudFormation automatically started rolling back the stack. Later, a DevOps engineer found that the application remained unavailable and the stack was in the `UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED` state.  
  
Which combination of actions should the DevOps engineer take to allow the stack rollback to finish successfully? (Choose two.)

options.text: Attach the AWSCIoudFormationFullAccess IAM policy to the AWS CloudFormation role.
Automatically recover the stack resources by using AWS CloudFormation drift detection.
Issue a ContinueUpdateRollback command from the AWS CloudFormation console or the AWS CLI.
Manually adjust the resources to match the expectations of the stack.
Update the existing AWS CloudFormation stack by using the original template.

questions.explanation:
For an `UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED` stack, manually synchronize any affected resources with the original stack template so CloudFormation can restore the expected prior state. Then invoke `ContinueUpdateRollback` from the CloudFormation console or AWS CLI to resume the rollback and move the stack toward `UPDATE_ROLLBACK_COMPLETE`.

**Learn more:** [Troubleshooting CloudFormation – Update rollback failed](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/troubleshooting.html) · [ContinueUpdateRollback API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/APIReference/API_ContinueUpdateRollback.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An Amazon EC2 instance runs in a Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) and must download an object from a restricted Amazon S3 bucket. When the DevOps engineer attempts the download, an `AccessDenied` error is returned.  
  
What could cause this error? (Choose two.)

options.text: The S3 bucket default encryption is enabled
There is an error in the S3 bucket policy
The object has been moved to Amazon Glacier
There is an error in the IAM role configuration
S3 versioning is enabled

questions.explanation:
Reading an Amazon S3 object requires `s3:GetObject` permission for the requesting principal. An incorrect bucket policy can deny or omit the required access, and an EC2 instance’s IAM role can likewise lack the necessary permission or be configured incorrectly. CloudFormation will be used to create a template for the development environments.  
  
Which approach will satisfy these requirements and quickly deliver consistent AWS environments for Developers?

options.text: Use Fn::ImportValue intrinsic functions in the Resources section of the template to retrieve Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) and subnet values. Use CloudFormation StackSets for the development environments, using the Count input parameter to indicate the number of environments needed. use the UpdateStackSet command to update existing development environments.

Use the CreateChangeSet and ExecuteChangeSet commands to update existing development environments.

Define the development resources in the order they need to be created in the CloudFormation nested stacks. questions.explanation:
Nested stacks let common infrastructure components be organized into reusable CloudFormation templates. A consuming stack retrieves VPC and subnet outputs exported by the separately deployed networking stack with `Fn::ImportValue` in the properties of the relevant nested-stack resources. CloudFormation change sets support reviewing and executing updates across a nested stack hierarchy.

A company’s application is presently deployed in a single AWS Region. The company recently opened a new office on another continent, and users in that office are encountering high latency. The company’s application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and uses Amazon DynamoDB as its database layer. The instances run in an EC2 Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. A DevOps Engineer must minimize application response times and improve availability for users in both Regions.  
  
Which combination of actions should be performed to resolve the latency issues? (Choose three.)

options.text: Create a new DynamoDB table in the new Region with cross-Region replication enabled.
Create new ALB and Auto Scaling group global resources and configure the new ALB to direct traffic to the new Auto Scaling group.
Create new ALB and Auto Scaling group resources in the new Region and configure the new ALB to direct traffic to the new Auto Scaling group.
Create Amazon Route 53 records, health checks, and latency-based routing policies to route to the ALB.
Create Amazon Route 53 aliases, health checks, and failover routing policies to route to the ALB.
Convert the DynamoDB table to a global table.

questions.explanation:
A Regional ALB and EC2 Auto Scaling group must be deployed in the new Region to serve that office locally. Route 53 latency-based records route users to the endpoint in the AWS Region with the lowest latency, while health checks support routing only to healthy endpoints. DynamoDB global tables replicate data across Regions and allow local replicas to serve reads and writes, improving both response time and multi-Region availability.

**Learn more:** [Latency-based routing - Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-latency.html) · [Routing traffic to an ELB load balancer - Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-to-elb-load-balancer.html)

Use an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to send alarm notices to the security team.

Create an Amazon S3 bucket for log files. Configure the VPC flow log to capture all traffic and to send the data to the S3 bucket. Configure Amazon QuickSight to accept data from Athena and to publish the data as a dashboard that the security team can access. Create a threshold alert of 1 for successful access. Configure the alert to automatically notify the security team as frequently as possible when the alert threshold is met.

Create an Amazon S3 bucket for log files. Configure the VPC flow log to capture accepted traffic and to send the data to the S3 bucket. Configure an Amazon OpenSearch Service duster and domain for the log files. Create an AWS Lambda function to retrieve the logs from the S3 bucket, format the logs, and load the logs into the OpenSearch Service cluster. Schedule the Lambda function to run every 5 minutes. Configure an alert and condition in OpenSearch Service to send alerts to the security team through an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic when access from the IP addresses on the deny list is detected.

Create a log group in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Create an Amazon S3 bucket to hold query results. Configure the VPC flow log to capture all traffic and to send the data to the log group. Deploy an Amazon Athena CloudWatch connector in AWS Lambda. Connect the connector to the log group. Configure Athena to periodically query for all accepted traffic from the IP addresses on the deny list and to store the results in the S3 bucket. Configure an S3 event notification to automatically notify the security team through an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic when new objects are added to the S3 bucket.

questions.explanation:
Accepted VPC Flow Log records identify traffic that was permitted to reach the application, so filtering them for deny-listed source IP addresses provides the required evidence while avoiding the cost of logging rejected traffic. CloudWatch Logs metric filters convert matching log events into metrics, CloudWatch alarms can evaluate those metrics on a five-minute period, and Amazon SNS can deliver the automated notifications. This managed path avoids the added OpenSearch, Lambda, Athena, QuickSight, and S3 query-processing infrastructure. AWS documents this specific pattern of applying a CloudWatch metric filter and alarm to VPC Flow Logs.

**Learn more:** [Process flow log records in CloudWatch Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/process-records-cwl.html) · [Creating metrics from log events using filters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/MonitoringLogData.html)

An n-tier application needs a table in an Amazon RDS MySQL DB instance to be dropped and repopulated during every deployment. This process can require several minutes, and the web tier cannot come online until it has finished. Currently, the web tier is configured in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group, with instances terminated and replaced at each deployment. The MySQL table is populated by running a SQL query through an AWS CodeBuild job.  
  
What should be done to ensure the web tier does not come online before the database is fully configured?

options.text: Use Amazon Aurora as a drop-in replacement for RDS MySQL. Use snapshots to populate the table with the correct data.
Modify the launch configuration of the Auto Scaling group to pause user data execution for 600 seconds, allowing the table to be populated.
Use AWS Step Functions to monitor and maintain the state of data population. Mark the database in service before continuing with the deployment.
Use an EC2 Auto Scaling lifecycle hook to pause the configuration of the web tier until the table is populated.

questions.explanation:
An EC2 Auto Scaling launch lifecycle hook places replacement web instances in a wait state until the database-population process completes. Completing the lifecycle action only after the CodeBuild SQL job succeeds lets the instances proceed to service, preventing them from receiving traffic against an incompletely configured database.

**Learn more:** [Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling lifecycle hooks](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/lifecycle-hooks.html) · [Complete a lifecycle action in an Auto Scaling group](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/completing-lifecycle-hooks.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company plans to use AWS CloudFormation to deploy infrastructure. The company has strict resource and tagging requirements and wants to restrict deployments to two Regions. Developers must be able to deploy multiple versions of the same application.  
  
Which solution ensures that resources are deployed according to company policy?

options.text: Create AWS Trusted Advisor checks to find and remediate unapproved CloudFormation StackSets.
Create a CloudFormation drift detection operation to find and remediate unapproved CloudFormation StackSets.
Create CloudFormation StackSets with approved CloudFormation templates.
Create AWS Service Catalog products with approved CloudFormation templates.

questions.explanation:
AWS Service Catalog provides governed self-service provisioning through administrator-approved CloudFormation product templates. Products support distinct versions, and TagOptions can apply and enforce a consistent tagging taxonomy for provisioned products. Making the catalog products available only in the permitted Regions restricts developer provisioning to those Regions.

**Learn more:** [Managing Versions - AWS Service Catalog](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/servicecatalog/latest/adminguide/managing-versions.html) · [AWS Service Catalog TagOption Library](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/servicecatalog/latest/adminguide/tagoptions.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A DevOps engineer uses AWS CodePipeline and AWS CodeBuild to build a CI/CD pipeline for a serverless application based on the AWS Serverless Application Model (AWS SAM). The source, build, and test steps are complete. The DevOps engineer has also created two pipeline deployment stages that use AWS CloudFormation as the action provider. One stage uses the **Create or replace a change set** action mode, and the other uses the **Execute a change set** action mode.  
  
The DevOps engineer must pass parameters to a CloudFormation stack during deployment without altering the code or pipeline structure.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Set the –parameter-overrides option in the sam deploy command when the CodeBuild stage is invoked.
Add all parameters in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Use dynamic references to specify template values in Parameter Store.
In the deployment stage where the
In the deployment stage where the

questions.explanation:
CloudFormation parameter values must be supplied when the change set is created, because the change set records the stack update that will later be executed. CodePipeline’s `ParameterOverrides` configuration accepts a JSON object for template parameters; placing it on the `CHANGE_SET_REPLACE` action ensures those values are included in the generated change set.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A security assessment found that an AWS CodeBuild project downloads a database-population script from an Amazon S3 bucket through an unauthenticated request. The security team prohibits unauthenticated requests to S3 buckets for this project.  
  
How can this problem be resolved in the **MOST** secure way?

options.text: Add the bucket name to the AllowedBuckets section of the CodeBuild project settings. Update the build spec to use the AWS CLI to download the database population script.
Modify the S3 bucket settings to enable HTTPS basic authentication and specify a token. Update the build spec to use cURL to pass the token and download the database population script.

Remove unauthenticated access from the S3 bucket with a bucket policy. Modify the service role for the CodeBuild project to include Amazon S3 access. Use the AWS CLI to download the database population script.
Remove unauthenticated access from the S3 bucket with a bucket policy. Use the AWS CLI to download the database population script using an IAM access key and a secret access key.

questions.explanation:
AWS CodeBuild uses its service role to perform AWS operations on the build's behalf. Removing public access with an S3 bucket policy and granting the CodeBuild service role only the necessary S3 read permissions enables an authenticated AWS CLI download using temporary role credentials, following least privilege. Static IAM access keys should not be supplied to the build.

**Learn more:** [Allow CodeBuild to interact with other AWS services](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/setting-up-service-role.html)

",["$","p",null,{"children":"The security team believes that part of the application’s demand might originate from users whose IP addresses are on a deny list. The security team gives the deny list to a DevOps engineer. If any IP addresses on the deny list access the application, the security team requires automated notification in near real time so that it can document the need for additional security. The DevOps engineer creates a VPC flow log for the production VPC."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":["Which additional set of steps should the DevOps engineer take to meet these requirements in the ",["$","strong",null,{"children":"MOST cost-effective"}]," way?"]}],"
",["$","$L55",null,{"choices":{"A":"Create a log group in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Configure the VPC flow log to capture accepted traffic and to send the data to the log group. Create an Amazon CloudWatch metric filter for IP addresses on the deny list. Create a CloudWatch alarm with the metric filter as input. Set the period to 5 minutes and the datapoints to alarm to 1. Use an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to send alarm notices to the security team.","B":"Create an Amazon S3 bucket for log files. Configure the VPC flow log to capture all traffic and to send the data to the S3 bucket. Configure Amazon Athena to return all log files in the S3 bucket for IP addresses on the deny list. Configure Amazon QuickSight to accept data from Athena and to publish the data as a dashboard that the security team can access. Create a threshold alert of 1 for successful access. Configure the alert to automatically notify the security team as frequently as possible when the alert threshold is met.","C":"Create an Amazon S3 bucket for log files. Configure the VPC flow log to capture accepted traffic and to send the data to the S3 bucket. Configure an Amazon OpenSearch Service duster and domain for the log files. Create an AWS Lambda function to retrieve the logs from the S3 bucket, format the logs, and load the logs into the OpenSearch Service cluster. Schedule the Lambda function to run every 5 minutes. Configure an alert and condition in OpenSearch Service to send alerts to the security team through an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic when access from the IP addresses on the deny list is detected.","D":"Create a log group in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Create an Amazon S3 bucket to hold query results. Configure the VPC flow log to capture all traffic and to send the data to the log group. Deploy an Amazon Athena CloudWatch connector in AWS Lambda. Connect the connector to the log group. Configure Athena to periodically query for all accepted traffic from the IP addresses on the deny list and to store the results in the S3 bucket. Configure an S3 event notification to automatically notify the security team through an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic when new objects are added to the S3 bucket."},"correctAnswer":"A","explanation":"Accepted VPC Flow Log records identify traffic that was permitted to reach the application, so filtering them for deny-listed source IP addresses provides the required evidence while avoiding the cost of logging rejected traffic. CloudWatch Logs metric filters convert matching log events into metrics, CloudWatch alarms can evaluate those metrics on a five-minute period, and Amazon SNS can deliver the automated notifications. This managed path avoids the added OpenSearch, Lambda, Athena, QuickSight, and S3 query-processing infrastructure. AWS documents this specific pattern of applying a CloudWatch metric filter and alarm to VPC Flow Logs.

A DevOps engineer needs a solution to migrate an application from on premises to AWS. The application runs on Linux and must run on particular versions of Apache Tomcat, HAProxy, and Varnish Cache to operate correctly. Its operating system-level parameters need tuning. The solution must provide a way to automate deployment of new application versions. The infrastructure must scale, and failed servers must be replaced automatically.  
  
Which solution should the DevOps engineer use?

options.text: Upload the application as a Docker image that contains all the necessary software to Amazon ECR. Create an Amazon ECS cluster using an AWS Fargate launch type and an Auto Scaling group. Create an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that uses Amazon ECR as a source and Amazon ECS as a deployment provider.

Upload the application code to an AWS CodeCommit repository with a saved configuration file to configure and install the software. Create an AWS Elastic Beanstalk web server tier and a load balanced-type environment that uses the Tomcat solution stack. Create an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that uses CodeCommit as a source and Elastic Beanstalk as a deployment provider.

Upload the application code to an AWS CodeCommit repository with a set of .ebextensions files to configure and install the software. Create an AWS Elastic Beanstalk worker tier environment that uses the Tomcat solution stack. Create an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that uses CodeCommit as a source and Elastic Beanstalk as a deployment provider.

Upload the application code to an AWS CodeCommit repository with an appspec.yml file to configure and install the necessary software. Create an AWS CodeDeploy deployment group associated with an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group. Create an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that uses CodeCommit as a source and CodeDeploy as a deployment provider.

questions.explanation:
AWS CodeDeploy on the EC2/On-Premises compute platform uses an `appspec.yml` file to map deployment files and run lifecycle-hook scripts. Those scripts can install and configure the required Linux software versions, tune operating-system parameters, and deploy later application revisions. An Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group scales capacity and automatically launches replacement instances when instances are unhealthy.

**Learn more:** [CodeDeploy AppSpec file reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/reference-appspec-file.html) · [AppSpec hooks section for CodeDeploy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/reference-appspec-file-structure-hooks.html)

A company is reviewing its IAM policies. A policy written by the DevOps engineer has been identified as too permissive. The policy is used by an AWS Lambda function that sends a stop command to Amazon EC2 instances tagged `Environment: NonProduction` during the weekend. The current policy is:  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783829517072-zbhp8igf.png)  
  
What changes should the engineer make to implement least-privilege permissions? (Choose three.)

options.text: ![](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783829520578-b4p7hirr.png)
Change “Resource”: “*” to “Resource”: “arn:aws:ec2:*:*:instance/*”
![](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783829524408-9q2d91p9.png)
![](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783829528017-notg4b38.png)
Change “Action”: “ec2:*” to “Action”: “ec2:StopInstances”
![](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783829532006-igbcg3rn.png)

questions.explanation:
Least privilege requires allowing only `ec2:StopInstances`, limiting the resource to EC2 instance ARNs, and requiring the target instance’s `Environment` resource tag to equal `NonProduction`. This prevents the role from performing other EC2 actions or stopping instances outside the intended tagged environment.

**Learn more:** [Controlling access to AWS resources using tags](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_tags.html) · [Amazon EC2 actions, resources, and condition keys](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/service-authorization/latest/reference/list_amazonec2.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is developing a web and mobile application that uses a serverless architecture powered by AWS Lambda and Amazon API Gateway. The company wants to fully automate backend Lambda deployment based on code pushed to the appropriate environment branch in an AWS CodeCommit repository.  
  
The deployment must include:  
  
- Separate environment pipelines for testing and production  
- Automatic deployment for test environments only  
  
Which steps should be taken to satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Configure a new AWS CodePipeline service. Create a CodeCommit repository for each environment. Set up CodePipeline to retrieve the source code from the appropriate repository. Set up the deployment step to deploy the Lambda functions with AWS CloudFormation.

Create two AWS CodePipeline configurations for test and production environments. Configure the production pipeline to have a manual approval step. Create a CodeCommit repository for each environment. Set up each CodePipeline to retrieve the source code from the appropriate repository. Set up the deployment step to deploy the Lambda functions with AWS CloudFormation.

Create two AWS CodePipeline configurations for test and production environments. Configure the production pipeline to have a manual approval step. Create one CodeCommit repository with a branch for each environment. Set up each CodePipeline to retrieve the source code from the appropriate branch in the repository. Set up the deployment step to deploy the Lambda functions with AWS CloudFormation.

Create an AWS CodeBuild configuration for test and production environments. Configure the production pipeline to have a manual approval step. Create one CodeCommit repository with a branch for each environment. Push the Lambda function code to an Amazon S3 bucket. Set up the deployment step to deploy the Lambda functions from the S3 bucket.

questions.explanation:
AWS CodePipeline can be configured with a CodeCommit repository and a specific branch as its source, and it starts when a new commit is made to that configured branch. Two pipelines can therefore use separate test and production branches in one repository. A manual approval action in the production pipeline prevents production deployment from proceeding automatically, while the test pipeline can deploy without that gate. AWS CloudFormation is a supported CodePipeline deployment provider and can deploy Lambda resources.

**Learn more:** [CodeCommit source action reference - AWS CodePipeline](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/action-reference-CodeCommit.html) · [Add a manual approval action to a pipeline in CodePipeline](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/approvals-action-add.html)

A company has a single-page application developed with Angular. A DevOps engineer must automate deployments of the application to a website the company hosts on Amazon S3. The solution must provide source-code version control and allow developers to conduct peer reviews.  
  
Which combination of steps meets these requirements? (Choose three.)

options.text: Create an AWS CodeCommit repository to store the source code. Create an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that has a source of the CodeCommit repository.
Create an S3 bucket to act as the source for developers to upload their source code. Create an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that has the S3 bucket as the source.
In the CodePipeline pipeline, configure an AWS CodeBuild phase that compiles the source code and produces build artifacts.
In the CodePipeline pipeline, configure an AWS CodeDeploy phase that compiles the source code, produces build artifacts, and then deploys the website.
In the CodePipeline pipeline, configure an AWS AppConfig deploy action that deploys the build artifacts to the S3 website bucket.
In the CodePipeline pipeline, configure an S3 deploy action that deploys the build artifacts to the S3 website bucket.

questions.explanation:
AWS CodeCommit supplies Git source control and pull requests that let developers review and comment on code changes. A CodePipeline source action can use the CodeCommit repository, a CodeBuild build action can compile the Angular source and create build artifacts, and an Amazon S3 deploy action publishes those artifacts to the S3 website bucket.

**Learn more:** [Working with pull requests in AWS CodeCommit repositories](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/pull-requests.html) · [AWS CodeBuild build and test action reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/action-reference-CodeBuild.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is deploying a well-architected design for its globally available API stack. The design must provide both high reliability and fast response times for users in North America and Europe.  
  
The API stack has these three tiers:  
  
- Amazon API Gateway  
- AWS Lambda  
- Amazon DynamoDB  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure Amazon Route 53 to point to API Gateway APIs in North America and Europe using health checks. Configure the APIs to forward requests to a Lambda function in that Region. Configure the Lambda functions to retrieve and update the data in a DynamoDB table in the same Region as the Lambda function.

Configure Amazon Route 53 to point to API Gateway APIs in North America and Europe using latency-based routing and health checks. Configure the APIs to forward requests to a Lambda function in that Region. Configure the Lambda functions to retrieve and update the data in a DynamoDB global table.

Configure Amazon Route 53 to point to API Gateway in North America, create a disaster recovery API in Europe, and configure both APIs to forward requests to the Lambda functions in that Region. Retrieve the data from a DynamoDB global table. Deploy a Lambda function to check the North America API health every 5 minutes. In the event of a failure, update Route 53 to point to the disaster recovery API.

Configure Amazon Route 53 to point to API Gateway API in North America using latency-based routing. Configure the API to forward requests to the Lambda function in the Region nearest to the user. Configure the Lambda function to retrieve and updathe data in a DynamoDB table.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing sends users to the configured AWS Region with the lowest latency, and health checks allow DNS to avoid unhealthy regional endpoints. Deploying API Gateway and Lambda in both Regions provides regional processing, while DynamoDB global tables provide multi-active, multi-Region replication with fast local reads and writes and allow a replica in either Region to serve requests. This combination provides low response times and multi-Region resilience.

**Learn more:** [Latency-based routing - Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-latency.html) · [Global tables - multi-active, multi-Region replication - Amazon DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/GlobalTables.html)

A company uses AWS CodeCommit for source control and wants to automate its continuous integration and continuous delivery pipeline on AWS for its development environment. The company has three requirements:  
  
1. A legal and security review must be performed for every code change to ensure that sensitive information is not exposed through the source code.  
2. Each change must undergo unit testing.  
3. Each change must undergo a suite of functional tests to verify functionality.  
  
Additionally, the company has the following automation requirements:  
  
1. Code changes must automatically initiate the CI/CD pipeline.  
2. Any pipeline failure must notify [email protected].  
3. Approval must be required to stage the assets to Amazon S3 after testing has completed.  
  
What should a DevOps Engineer do to meet all these requirements while following CI/CD best practices?

options.text: Commit to the development branch and trigger AWS CodePipeline from the development branch. Make an individual stage in CodePipeline for security review, unit tests, functional tests, and manual approval. Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics to detect changes in pipeline stages and Amazon SES for emailing [email protected].

Commit to mainline and trigger AWS CodePipeline from mainline. Make an individual stage in CodePipeline for security review, unit tests, functional tests, and manual approval. Use AWS CloudTrail logs to detect changes in pipeline stages and Amazon SNS for emailing [email protected].

Commit to the development branch and trigger AWS CodePipeline from the development branch. Make an individual stage in CodePipeline for security review, unit tests, functional tests, and manual approval. Use Amazon CloudWatch Events to detect changes in pipeline stages and Amazon SNS for emailing [email protected].

Commit to mainline and trigger AWS CodePipeline from mainline. Make an individual stage in CodePipeline for security review, unit tests, functional tests, and manual approval. Use Amazon CloudWatch Events to detect changes in pipeline stages and Amazon SES for emailing [email protected].

questions.explanation:
AWS CodePipeline supports source, test, approval, and deploy actions arranged in ordered stages. A CodeCommit source branch can automatically start the pipeline; separate review and test stages enforce the required security, unit, and functional gates. A manual approval action pauses execution before an Amazon S3 deploy action. CloudWatch Events, now Amazon EventBridge, can detect CodePipeline state changes, and Amazon SNS can send the resulting failure notification to an email subscriber.

**Learn more:** [Create a pipeline, stages, and actions - AWS CodePipeline](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/pipelines-create.html) · [Add a manual approval action to a pipeline in CodePipeline](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/approvals-action-add.html)

A company stores 100 GB of log data in an Amazon S3 bucket in `.csv` format. SQL developers need to query this data and produce graphs to visualize it.  
  
They also require an efficient, automated method to store metadata from the `.csv` file.  
  
Which combination of steps should be taken to satisfy these requirements with the **LEAST** effort? (Choose three.)

options.text: Filter the data through AWS X-Ray to visualize the data.
Filter the data through Amazon QuickSight to visualize the data.
Query the data with Amazon Athena.
Query the data with Amazon Redshift.
Use AWS Glue as the persistent metadata store.
Use Amazon S3 as the persistent metadata store.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Athena queries data stored directly in Amazon S3 using SQL. Amazon QuickSight creates graphical visualizations, including charts and graphs. The AWS Glue Data Catalog is a persistent metadata repository, and AWS Glue crawlers can automatically infer the schema of CSV files in Amazon S3 and write that metadata to the catalog.

**Learn more:** [Data discovery and cataloging in AWS Glue](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/catalog-and-crawler.html) · [Using crawlers to populate the AWS Glue Data Catalog](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/add-crawler.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates a custom-built application that processes records. Every component runs on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. Processing each record consists of a compute-intensive, multistep sequential operation. Every step always finishes within 5 minutes or less.  
  
The current system has a limitation: if any step fails, the application must process the record again from the start. The company wants to update the architecture so that it reprocesses only failed steps.  
  
What is the **MOST** operationally efficient solution that fulfills these requirements?

options.text: Create a web application to write records to Amazon S3. Use S3 Event Notifications to publish to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Use an EC2 instance to poll Amazon SNS and start processing. Save intermediate results to Amazon S3 to pass on to the next step.

Perform the processing steps by using logic in the application. Convert the application code to run in a container. Use AWS Fargate to manage the container instances. Configure the container to invoke itself to pass the state from one step to the next.
Create a web application to pass records to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Decouple the processing by using the Kinesis data stream and AWS Lambda functions.
Create a web application to pass records to AWS Step Functions. Decouple the processing into Step Functions tasks and AWS Lambda functions.

questions.explanation:
AWS Step Functions orchestrates sequential tasks while maintaining workflow execution state. Its task-level retry and error-handling capabilities allow only a failed AWS Lambda task to be retried, while completed tasks remain complete. Because each step finishes in 5 minutes or less, each can run within Lambda’s maximum 15-minute invocation timeout.

**Learn more:** [Handling errors in Step Functions workflows](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/concepts-error-handling.html) · [Configure Lambda function timeout](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-timeout.html)

A company has migrated its container-based applications to Amazon EKS and wants to set up automated email notifications. Notifications sent to each email address concern specific activities associated with EKS components. The solution will use Amazon SNS topics and an AWS Lambda function to assess incoming log events and publish messages to the appropriate SNS topic.  
  
Which logging solution supports these requirements?

options.text: Enable Amazon CloudWatch Logs to log the EKS components. Create a CloudWatch subscription filter for each component with Lambda as the subscription feed destination.
Enable Amazon CloudWatch Logs to log the EKS components. Create CloudWatch Logs Insights queries linked to Amazon EventBridge events that invoke Lambda.
Enable Amazon S3 logging for the EKS components. Configure an Amazon CloudWatch subscription filter for each component with Lambda as the subscription feed destination.
Enable Amazon S3 logging for the EKS components. Configure S3 PUT Object event notifications with AWS Lambda as the destination.

questions.explanation:

A CloudWatch Logs subscription filter can forward matching log events to AWS Lambda in real time; the function can evaluate those events and publish to the relevant Amazon SNS topic for email delivery.

**Learn more:** [Send control plane logs to CloudWatch Logs - Amazon EKS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/control-plane-logs.html) · [Log group-level subscription filters - Amazon CloudWatch Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/SubscriptionFilters.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company develops and maintains a web application that uses Amazon EC2 instances and an Amazon RDS for SQL Server DB instance in a single Availability Zone. The resources must run only when new deployments are tested by using AWS CodePipeline. Testing takes place one or more times each week, and every test runs for 2–3 hours. A DevOps engineer needs a solution that does not alter the architecture components.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements in the **MOST** cost-effective way?

options.text: Convert the RDS database to an Amazon Aurora Serverless database. Use an AWS Lambda function to start and stop the EC2 instances before and after tests.
Put the EC2 instances into an Auto Scaling group. Schedule scaling to run at the start of the deployment tests.
Replace the EC2 instances with EC2 Spot Instances and the RDS database with an RDS Reserved Instance.
Subscribe Amazon CloudWatch Events to CodePipeline to trigger AWS Systems Manager Automation documents that start and stop all EC2 and RDS instances before and after deployment tests.

questions.explanation:
Stopping the EC2 instances and the single-AZ RDS for SQL Server DB instance when tests are not running eliminates EC2 and RDS DB instance-hour charges while preserving the existing components and configuration. RDS supports temporarily stopping and starting Microsoft SQL Server DB instances, and AWS CodePipeline sends execution events to Amazon EventBridge. EventBridge can invoke AWS Systems Manager Automation runbooks, enabling the start and stop actions to be tied to the deployment-test workflow.

**Learn more:** [Stopping an Amazon RDS DB instance temporarily](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_StopInstance.html) · [AWS CodePipeline events - Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/ref/events-ref-codepipeline.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company developed an AWS Lambda function to process orders received through an API. The company uses AWS CodeDeploy to deploy the Lambda function as the final stage of a CI/CD pipeline.  
  
A DevOps Engineer has observed intermittent ordering API failures for a few seconds following deployment. After investigating, the DevOps Engineer believes the failures occur because database changes have not fully propagated before the Lambda function starts to execute.  
  
How should the DevOps Engineer address this?

options.text: Add a BeforeAllowTraffic hook to the AppSpec file that tests and waits for any necessary database changes before traffic can flow to the new version of the Lambda function
Add an AfterAllowTraffic hook to the AppSpec file that forces traffic to wait for any pending database changes before allowing the new version of the Lambda function to respond
Add a BeforeInstall hook to the AppSpec file that tests and waits for any necessary database changes before deploying the new version of the Lambda function
Add a ValidateService hook to the AppSpec file that inspects incoming traffic and rejects the payload if dependent services, such as the database, are not yet ready

questions.explanation:
For an AWS Lambda deployment, the `BeforeAllowTraffic` lifecycle hook runs before CodeDeploy shifts production traffic to the deployed Lambda function version. A validation hook can wait for and verify database-change propagation, allowing the traffic shift only after the dependency is ready. AWS Lambda CodeDeploy deployments provide `BeforeAllowTraffic` and `AfterAllowTraffic` hooks; the latter occurs after traffic has already shifted.

**Learn more:** [AppSpec 'hooks' section for an AWS Lambda deployment](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/reference-appspec-file-structure-hooks.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company that uses electronic health records operates a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances running the Amazon Linux operating system. To meet patient-privacy requirements, the company must maintain continuous patch compliance for the operating system and applications running on those EC2 instances.  
  
How can deployment of operating-system and application patches be automated by using both a default and a custom repository?

options.text: Use AWS Systems Manager to create a new patch baseline including the custom repository. Run the AWS-RunPatchBaseline document using the run command to verify and install patches.
Use AWS Direct Connect to integrate the corporate repository and deploy the patches using Amazon CloudWatch scheduled events, then use the CloudWatch dashboard to create reports.
Use yum-config-manager to add the custom repository under /etc/yum.repos.d and run yum-config-manager-enable to activate the repository.
Use AWS Systems Manager to create a new patch baseline including the corporate repository. Run the AWS-AmazonLinuxDefaultPatchBaseline document using the run command to verify and install patches.

questions.explanation:
AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager supports custom patch baselines for Amazon Linux, allowing approved patches to be sourced from a custom repository. The `AWS-RunPatchBaseline` command document performs patch scanning and installation against the applicable baseline, enabling centralized patch deployment and compliance reporting across managed EC2 instances.

**Learn more:** [Predefined and custom patch baselines - AWS Systems Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/patch-manager-predefined-and-custom-patch-baselines.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company requires a 2-hour RPO and a 10-minute RTO for its data and application at all times. An application uses a MySQL database and Amazon EC2 web servers. The development team needs a failover and disaster-recovery strategy.  
  
Which combination of deployment strategies will satisfy these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create an Amazon Aurora cluster in one Availability Zone across multiple Regions as the data store. Use Aurora's automatic recovery capabilities in the event of a disaster.
Create an Amazon Aurora global database in two Regions as the data store. In the event of a failure, promote the secondary Region as the master for the application.
Create an Amazon Aurora multi-master cluster across multiple Regions as the data store. Use a Network Load Balancer to balance the database traffic in different Regions.

Set up the application in two Regions and use Amazon Route 53 failover-based routing that points to the Application Load Balancers in both Regions. Use health checks to determine the availability in a given Region. Use Auto Scaling groups in each Region to adjust capacity based on demand.

Set up the application in two Regions and use a multi-Region Auto Scaling group behind Application Load Balancers to manage the capacity based on demand. In the event of a disaster, adjust the Auto Scaling group's desired instance count to increase baseline capacity in the failover Region.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Aurora Global Database maintains a secondary database cluster in another AWS Region and supports cross-Region failover for Regional disasters. Aurora Global Database recovery objectives are typically an RPO measured in seconds and an RTO in the order of minutes. Deploying the application in both Regions behind Regional Application Load Balancers, with Amazon Route 53 failover routing and health checks, redirects traffic to the healthy Region while Auto Scaling groups provide Regional capacity.

**Learn more:** [Using switchover or failover in Amazon Aurora Global Database](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-global-database-disaster-recovery.html) · [Creating Amazon Route 53 health checks](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-failover.html)

An e-commerce company runs a web application in an AWS Elastic Beanstalk environment. In recent months, the average load on the Amazon EC2 instances has increased to accommodate additional traffic.  
  
The company wants to improve the environment’s scalability and resilience. The Development team has been asked to decouple long-running tasks from the environment when those tasks can run asynchronously. Examples include confirmation emails when users register on the platform and image or video processing. Some periodic tasks that currently run within the web server should also be offloaded.  
  
What is the **MOST** time-efficient and integrated way to accomplish this?

options.text: Create an Amazon SQS queue and send the tasks that should be decoupled from the Elastic Beanstalk web server environment to the SQS queue. Create a fleet of EC2 instances under an Auto Scaling group. Use an AMI that contains the application to process the asynchronous tasks, configure the application to listen for messages within the SQS queue, and create periodic tasks by placing those into the cron in the operating system. Create an environment variable within the Elastic Beanstalk environment with a value pointing to the SQS queue endpoint.

Create a second Elastic Beanstalk worker tier environment and deploy the application to process the asynchronous tasks there. Send the tasks that should be decoupled from the original Elastic Beanstalk web server environment to the auto-generated Amazon SQS queue by the Elastic Beanstalk worker environment. Place a cron.yaml file within the root of the application source bundle for the worker environment for periodic tasks. Use environment links to link the web server environment with the worker environment.

Create a second Elastic Beanstalk web server tier environment and deploy the application to process the asynchronous tasks. Send the tasks that should be decoupled from the original Elastic Beanstalk web server to the auto-generated Amazon SQS queue by the second Elastic Beanstalk web server tier environment. Place a cron.yaml file within the root of the application source bundle for the second web server tier environment with the necessary periodic tasks. Use environment links to link both web server environments.

Create an Amazon SQS queue and send the tasks that should be decoupled from the Elastic Beanstalk web server environment to the SQS queue. Create a fleet of EC2 instances under an Auto Scaling group. Install and configure the application to listen for messages within the SQS queue from UserData and create periodic tasks by placing those into the cron in the operating system. Create an environment variable within the Elastic Beanstalk web server environment with a value pointing to the SQS queue endpoint.

questions.explanation:
An Elastic Beanstalk worker-tier environment is the managed pattern for background work. It processes messages from an Amazon SQS queue independently of the web-server tier, enabling separate scaling and preventing long-running work from consuming web-server capacity. Elastic Beanstalk can automatically create the worker queue, `cron.yaml` schedules periodic jobs onto that queue, and environment links let the web tier discover the worker queue endpoint without manually managing EC2 worker fleets or operating-system cron jobs.

**Learn more:** [Elastic Beanstalk worker environments](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/using-features-managing-env-tiers.html) · [Creating links between Elastic Beanstalk environments](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/environment-cfg-links.html)

A company has created a Node.js web application that exposes REST services for storing and retrieving time series data. The development team builds the web application on company laptops, tests it locally, and manually deploys it to one on-premises server that accesses a local MySQL database. The company will begin a trial in two weeks, during which the application will receive frequent updates in response to customer feedback. The following requirements must be satisfied:  
  
- The team must reliably build, test, and deploy new updates every day, with no downtime or performance degradation.  
- The application must scale to handle an unpredictable number of concurrent users during the trial.  
  
Which action will enable the team to meet these objectives quickly?

options.text: Create two Amazon Lightsail virtual private servers for Node.js; one for test and one for production. Build the Node.js application using existing processes and upload it to the new Lightsail test server using the AWS CLI. Test the application, and if it passes all tests, upload it to the production server. During the trial, monitor the production server usage, and if needed, increase performance by upgrading the instance type.

Develop an AWS CloudFormation template to create an Application Load Balancer and two Amazon EC2 instances with Amazon EBS (SSD) volumes in an Auto Scaling group with rolling updates enabled. Use AWS CodeBuild to build and test the Node.js application and store it in an Amazon S3 bucket. Use user-data scripts to install the application and the MySQL database on each EC2 instance. Update the stack to deploy new application versions.

Configure AWS Elastic Beanstalk to automatically build the application using AWS CodeBuild and to deploy it to a test environment that is configured to support auto scaling. Create a second Elastic Beanstalk environment for production. Use Amazon RDS to store data. When new versions of the applications have passed all tests, use Elastic Beanstalk 'swap cname' to promote the test environment to production.

Modify the application to use Amazon DynamoDB instead of a local MySQL database. Use AWS OpsWorks to create a stack for the application with a DynamoDB layer, an Application Load Balancer layer, and an Amazon EC2 instance layer. Use a Chef recipe to build the application and a Chef recipe to deploy the application to the EC2 instance layer. Use custom health checks to run unit tests on each instance with rollback on failure.

questions.explanation:
Elastic Beanstalk provides load-balanced environments backed by Auto Scaling, so application capacity can increase or decrease with demand. A separate test environment can receive and validate a new version, while an Elastic Beanstalk CNAME swap redirects production traffic to that environment as a blue/green deployment without interrupting service. Amazon RDS keeps the relational database independent of the application environments, which is required for this deployment pattern.

**Learn more:** [Blue/Green deployments with Elastic Beanstalk](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/using-features.CNAMESwap.html) · [Auto Scaling your Elastic Beanstalk environment instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/using-features.managing.as.html)
