A company stores its purchase history in an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company needs other workloads running on AWS to respond to data changes in that table.  
  
The company has enabled a DynamoDB stream on the table. Three existing AWS Lambda functions have event source mappings configured for the DynamoDB stream. The company's application developers intend to add other applications that must respond to table changes. A DevOps engineer must design an architecture that provides this capability to the additional consumers.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements in the **MOST** operationally efficient way?

options.text: Create an Amazon EventBridge event bus. Create a new Lambda function that uses the existing DynamoDB stream as an event source. Configure the new Lambda function to post those events to the event bus. Update the original Lambda functions to react to events in the event bus. As other applications need the events, configure the applications to use the event bus as an event source.

Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SOS) queue. Create a new Lambda function that uses the existing DynamoDB stream as an event source. Configure the new Lambda function to post those events to the SOS queue. Update the original Lambda functions to react to entries in the SOS queue. As other applications need the events, configure the applications to use the SOS queue as an event source.

Create an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Create a new Lambda function that uses the existing DynamoDB stream as an event source. Configure the new Lambda function to post those events to the Kinesis data stream. Update the original Lambda functions to subscribe to records in the Kinesis data stream. As other applications need the events, configure the applications to use the Kinesis data stream as an event source.
Configure the DynamoDB table to use on-demand capacity mode. Increase the memory of the Lambda functions. Configure the Lambda functions to use provisioned concurrency.

questions.explanation:
DynamoDB Streams has a limit of two simultaneous consumers per shard, so directly attaching multiple Lambda consumers risks read throttling. Amazon EventBridge provides serverless event routing and fan-out: one consumer can publish the stream changes to an event bus, whose rules deliver matching events independently to the existing and future application targets. This avoids direct-stream consumer scaling and the operational overhead of managing a Kinesis-based distribution layer.

**Learn more:** [Integrating DynamoDB with Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/eventbridge-for-dynamodb.html) · [DynamoDB Streams and AWS Lambda triggers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Streams.Lambda.html)

A DevOps engineer has automated deployment of a web service by using AWS CodePipeline with these steps:  
  
1. An AWS CodeBuild project compiles the deployment artifact and runs unit tests.  
2. An AWS CodeDeploy deployment group deploys the web service to Amazon EC2 instances in the staging environment.  
3. A CodeDeploy deployment group deploys the web service to EC2 instances in the production environment.  
  
The quality assurance (QA) team requests permission to inspect the build artifact before deployment to the production environment takes place. The QA team wants to use an internal penetration-testing tool to perform manual tests. The tool is invoked through a REST API call.  
  
Which combination of actions should the DevOps engineer take to meet this request? (Choose two.)

options.text: Insert a manual approval action between the test actions and deployment actions of the pipeline.
Modify the buildspec.yml file for the compilation stage to require manual approval before completion.
Update the CodeDeploy deployment groups so that they require manual approval to proceed.
Update the pipeline to directly call the REST API for the penetration testing tool.
Update the pipeline to invoke a Lambda function that calls the REST API for the penetration testing tool.

questions.explanation:
A CodePipeline manual approval action stops the pipeline at the configured point until an authorized approver approves or rejects it, which provides QA a promotion gate before production deployment. A Lambda invoke action lets the pipeline execute custom code, and that Lambda function can call the penetration-testing tool’s REST API.

**Learn more:** [Add a manual approval action to a pipeline in CodePipeline](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/approvals-action-add.html) · [Invoke an AWS Lambda function in a pipeline in CodePipeline](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/actions-invoke-lambda-function.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has AWS accounts that belong to the same organization in AWS Organizations. Under the company’s security policy, IAM customer managed policies must be limited to specific actions and must not contain wildcard actions on wildcard resources.  
  
If an IAM customer managed policy is created or modified in any company AWS account to allow wildcard actions on resources that also use wildcards, the policy must be detached from every IAM user, role, or group to which it is attached. Individual AWS account administrators must be unable to prevent the policies from being removed.  
  
Which combination of steps meets these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Configure automatic remediation to run the AWSConfigRemediation-DetachIAMPolicy AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook.
Configure automatic remediation to invoke a custom AWS Lambda function to detach the IAM policy from the affected resources.
Configure automatic remediation to use AWS Systems Manager Run Command to detach the IAM policy from the affected resources.

Turn on AWS Config by using an AWS CloudFormation stack set that is created in a central account. Configure automatic deployment for the stack set, and specify the organization as the target. Configure the iam-policy-no-statements-with-full-access AWS Config managed rule in the central account.

Turn on AWS Config for the organization. Create a new AWS account. Configure the account as a delegated administrator account for AWS Config. Configure the iam-policy-no-statements-with-full-access AWS Config managed rule in the delegated administrator account.

questions.explanation:
The iam-policy-no-statements-with-full-access AWS Config managed rule flags customer managed policies that allow full (wildcard) access, and pairing it with automatic remediation using the AWSConfigRemediation-DetachIAMPolicy Systems Manager Automation runbook (option A) detaches the offending policy from every user, role, and group. To enforce this organization-wide while ensuring individual account administrators cannot disable or delete the control, you enable AWS Config for the organization and deploy the rule from a delegated administrator account (option E); organization Config rules and their remediation are managed centrally and cannot be modified by member-account admins. Option D is incorrect because it places the managed rule only in the central account (so it never evaluates member accounts), and CloudFormation StackSet-deployed resources can still be altered locally by an account admin. Options B and C are unnecessary custom mechanisms when the managed runbook already exists.

**Learn more:** [AWSConfigRemediation-DetachIAMPolicy runbook](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager-automation-runbooks/latest/userguide/automation-aws-detach-iam-policy.html) · [iam-policy-no-statements-with-full-access](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/iam-policy-no-statements-with-full-access.html) · [Using delegated admin for AWS Config](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/mt/using-delegated-admin-for-aws-config-operations-and-aggregation/)

A company is building a web application's infrastructure with AWS CloudFormation. The database engineering team manages the database resources in one CloudFormation template, while the software development team manages the web application resources in a separate CloudFormation template. As the application's scope expands, the software development team must use resources that the database engineering team maintains. However, both teams want to retain their own review and lifecycle-management processes. Both teams also need resource-level change-set reviews. The software development team wants to deploy changes to this template through its CI/CD pipeline.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a stack export from the database CloudFormation template and import those references into the web application CloudFormation template.
Create a CloudFormation nested stack to make cross-stack resource references and parameters available in both stacks.
Create a CloudFormation stack set to make cross-stack resource references and parameters available in both stacks.
Create input parameters in the web application CloudFormation template and pass resource names and IDs from the database stack.

questions.explanation:
CloudFormation cross-stack references let one independently managed stack expose selected resource outputs with `Export` and let another stack consume them with `Fn::ImportValue`. This preserves separate stacks, templates, deployment pipelines, and change-set reviews while providing a supported reference to database resources. Nested stacks are operated through a root stack hierarchy, and StackSets address multi-account or multi-Region deployments rather than this sharing pattern.

**Learn more:** [Refer to resource outputs in another CloudFormation stack](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/walkthrough-crossstackref.html) · [Fn::ImportValue](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/intrinsic-function-reference-importvalue.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is deploying an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster to run its workload. Its architecture will run multiple ECS services on the cluster. The architecture includes an Application Load Balancer at the front end and uses multiple target groups to route traffic.  
  
A DevOps engineer must collect application and access logs, then send the logs to an Amazon S3 bucket for near-real-time analysis.  
  
Which combination of steps must the DevOps engineer take to satisfy these requirements? (Choose three.)

options.text: Download the Amazon CloudWatch Logs container instance from AWS. Configure this instance as a task. Update the application service definitions to include the logging task
Install the Amazon CloudWatch Logs agent on the ECS instances. Change the logging driver in the ECS task definition to awslogs.

Use Amazon EventBridge to schedule an AWS Lambda function that will run every 60 seconds and will run the Amazon CloudWatch Logs create-export-task command. Then point the output to the logging S3 bucket.
Activate access logging on the ALB. Then point the ALB directly to the logging S3 bucket.
Activate access logging on the target groups that the ECS services use. Then send the logs directly to the logging S3 bucket.
Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream that has a destination of the logging S3 bucket. Then create an Amazon CloudWatch Logs subscription filter for Kinesis Data Firehose.

questions.explanation:
ECS containers can route their output to CloudWatch Logs with the `awslogs` logging driver. A CloudWatch Logs subscription filter can forward incoming log events to an Amazon Data Firehose delivery stream, which delivers them to Amazon S3 according to its configured buffer interval. Application Load Balancer access logging is enabled on the load balancer and stores access-log files in the specified S3 bucket.

**Learn more:** [Send Amazon ECS logs to CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/using_awslogs.html) · [Log group-level subscription filters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/SubscriptionFilters.html)

options.text: Create primary and secondary Amazon S3 buckets in two separate Availability Zones that are at least 500 miles (805 kilometers) apart. Use a bucket policy to enforce access to the buckets only through HTTPS. Use a bucket policy to enforce Amazon S3 SSE-C on all objects uploaded to the bucket. Configure cross- region replication between the two buckets.

Create primary and secondary Amazon S3 buckets in two separate AWS Regions that are at least 500 miles (805 kilometers) apart. Use a bucket policy to enforce access to the buckets only through HTTPS. Use a bucket policy to enforce S3-Managed Keys (SSE-S3) on all objects uploaded to the bucket. Configure cross-region replication between the two buckets.

Create primary and secondary Amazon S3 buckets in two separate AWS Regions that are at least 500 miles (805 kilometers) apart. Use an IAM role to enforce access to the buckets only through HTTPS. Use a bucket policy to enforce Amazon S3-Managed Keys (SSE-S3) on all objects uploaded to the bucket. Configure cross-region replication between the two buckets.

Create primary and secondary Amazon S3 buckets in two separate Availability Zones that are at least 500 miles (805 kilometers) apart. Use a bucket policy to enforce access to the buckets only through HTTPS. Use a bucket policy to enforce AWS KMS encryption on all objects uploaded to the bucket. Configure cross-region replication between the two buckets. Create a KMS Customer Master Key (CMK) in the primary region for encrypting objects.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication copies objects between buckets in different AWS Regions, allowing replicas to be placed the required distance apart. A bucket policy can deny non-HTTPS requests to enforce encryption in transit, and an SSE-S3 requirement encrypts uploaded objects at rest with Amazon S3 managed keys.

**Learn more:** [Security best practices for Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/security-best-practices.html) · [Replicating objects within and across Regions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication.html)

A DevOps engineer is evaluating the lowest-cost approach for implementing an image batch-processing cluster on AWS. The application cannot run in Docker containers and must operate on Amazon EC2. The batch job saves checkpoint data on NFS and can withstand interruptions. Configuring the cluster software from a generic EC2 Linux image requires 30 minutes.  
  
What is the **MOST** cost-effective solution?

options.text: Use Amazon EFS for checkpoint data. To complete the job, use an EC2 Auto Scaling group and an On-Demand pricing model to provision EC2 instances temporarily.
Use GlusterFS on EC2 instances for checkpoint data. To run the batch job, configure EC2 instances manually. When the job completes, shut down the instances manually.
Use Amazon EFS for checkpoint data. Use EC2 Fleet to launch EC2 Spot Instances, and utilize user data to configure the EC2 Linux instance on startup.
Use Amazon EFS for checkpoint data. Use EC2 Fleet to launch EC2 Spot Instances. Create a custom AMI for the cluster and use the latest AMI when creating instances.

questions.explanation:
EC2 Spot Instances are well suited to interruptible batch processing and reduce compute cost by using spare EC2 capacity. Amazon EFS provides a managed shared file system accessible by multiple EC2 instances through NFS, so checkpoint data persists across instance interruptions. Packaging the cluster software in a custom AMI eliminates the recurring 30-minute setup time for each launched instance; EC2 Fleet can provision the Spot capacity.

**Learn more:** [Spot Instances - Amazon EC2 User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/using-spot-instances.html) · [How Amazon EFS works - Amazon EFS User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/how-it-works.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates an application that stores logs in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. The company needs to archive the logs in Amazon S3. The logs are seldom accessed after 90 days and must be kept for 10 years.  
  
Which combination of actions should a DevOps engineer take to satisfy these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Configure a CloudWatch Logs subscription filter to use AWS Glue to transfer all logs to an S3 bucket.
Configure a CloudWatch Logs subscription filter to use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to stream all logs to an S3 bucket.
Configure a CloudWatch Logs subscription filter to stream all logs to an S3 bucket.
Configure the S3 bucket lifecycle policy to transition logs to S3 Glacier after 90 days and to expire logs after 3,650 days.
Configure the S3 bucket lifecycle policy to transition logs to Reduced Redundancy after 90 days and to expire logs after 3,650 days.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Data Firehose is a supported CloudWatch Logs subscription destination and can deliver matching log events to an Amazon S3 bucket. An S3 Lifecycle rule can transition objects to an S3 Glacier storage class after 90 days and expire them after 3,650 days, meeting the archival-access pattern and 10-year retention requirement.

**Learn more:** [Log group-level subscription filters - Amazon CloudWatch Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/SubscriptionFilters.html) · [Examples of S3 Lifecycle configurations - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/lifecycle-configuration-examples.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A production account requires that every Amazon EC2 instance that has been manually logged into be terminated within 24 hours. All applications in the production account use Auto Scaling groups with the Amazon CloudWatch Logs agent configured.  
  
How can this process be automated?

options.text: Create a CloudWatch Logs subscription to an AWS Step Functions application. Configure the function to add a tag to the EC2 instance that produced the login event and mark the instance to be decommissioned. Then create a CloudWatch Events rule to trigger a second AWS Lambda function once a day that will terminate all instances with this tag.

Create a CloudWatch alarm that will trigger on the login event. Send the notification to an Amazon SNS topic that the operations team is subscribed to, and have them terminate the EC2 instance within 24 hours.

Create a CloudWatch alarm that will trigger on the login event. Configure the alarm to send to an Amazon SQS queue. Use a group of worker instances to process messages from the queue, which then schedules the Amazon CloudWatch Events rule to trigger.

Create a CloudWatch Logs subscription in an AWS Lambda function. Configure the function to add a tag to the EC2 instance that produced the login event and mark the instance to be decommissioned. Create a CloudWatch Events rule to trigger a daily Lambda function that terminates all instances with this tag.

questions.explanation:
A CloudWatch Logs subscription filter can route matching login events to AWS Lambda for event-specific processing. Lambda can tag the EC2 instance associated with a manual login, and a daily scheduled CloudWatch Events (now Amazon EventBridge) rule can invoke another Lambda function to terminate all instances with that tag. This supplies both automatic detection and termination within the required period.

**Learn more:** [Log group-level subscription filters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/SubscriptionFilters.html) · [Concepts - Amazon CloudWatch Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/subscription-concepts.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A DevOps engineer plans to deploy a Ruby-based application to production. The application must interact with an Amazon RDS for MySQL database and provide automatic scaling and high availability. Data stored in the database is critical and must persist regardless of the application stack’s state.  
  
The DevOps engineer must establish an automated deployment strategy for the application that includes automatic rollbacks. The solution must also alert the application team if a deployment fails.  
  
Which combination of steps meets these requirements? (Choose three.)

options.text: Deploy the application on AWS Elastic Beanstalk. Deploy an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance as part of the Elastic Beanstalk configuration.
Deploy the application on AWS Elastic Beanstalk. Deploy a separate Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance outside of Elastic Beanstalk.
Configure a notification email address that alerts the application team in the AWS Elastic Beanstalk configuration.
Configure an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule to monitor AWS Health events. Use an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic as a target to alert the application team.
Use the immutable deployment method to deploy new application versions.
Use the rolling deployment method to deploy new application versions.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance deployed outside Elastic Beanstalk is independent of the Elastic Beanstalk environment lifecycle, so its data remains available if the environment is terminated. Elastic Beanstalk environment notifications can send email notifications through Amazon SNS when environment errors occur. Immutable deployments create a separate, full set of instances for the new version; if the new instances fail health checks, Elastic Beanstalk terminates them and leaves the original instances unchanged, effectively rolling back automatically.

**Learn more:** [Using Elastic Beanstalk with Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/AWSHowTo.RDS.html) · [Elastic Beanstalk environment notifications with Amazon SNS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/using-features.managing.sns.html)

A DevOps engineer is implementing governance controls for a company that requires its infrastructure to be located within the United States. The engineer must limit the AWS Regions that can be used and ensure an alert is sent as soon as possible if any activity outside the governance policy occurs. The controls must be automatically enabled for any new Region outside the United States (US).  
  
Which combination of actions meets these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create an AWS Organizations SCP that denies access to all non-global services in non-US Regions. Attach the policy to the root of the organization.
Configure AWS CloudTrail to send logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs and enable it for all Regions. Use a CloudWatch Logs metric filter to send an alert on any service activity in non-US Regions.

Use an AWS Lambda function that checks for AWS service activity and deploy it to all Regions. Write an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs the Lambda function every hour, sending an alert if activity is found in a non-US Region.
Use an AWS Lambda function to query Amazon Inspector to look for service activity in non-US Regions and send alerts if any activity is found.
Write an SCP using the aws:RequestedRegion condition key limiting access to US Regions. Apply the policy to all users, groups and roles.

questions.explanation:
An AWS Organizations SCP attached at the organization root can explicitly deny non-global service actions in non-US Regions for all governed accounts, providing preventive region control without needing individual principal policies. A multi-Region CloudTrail trail applies its configuration across enabled Regions, including a copied trail when an opt-in Region is enabled. Sending its events to CloudWatch Logs enables metric filters and alarms to promptly notify on activity that matches non-US Region criteria.

**Learn more:** [SCP syntax - AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps_syntax.html) · [Understanding multi-Region trails and opt-in Regions - AWS CloudTrail](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-multi-region-trails.html)

A company is rolling out a new application that uses Amazon EC2 instances. The company requires a solution to query application logs and AWS account API activity.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Use the Amazon CloudWatch agent to send logs from the EC2 instances to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Configure AWS CloudTrail to deliver the API logs to Amazon S3. Use CloudWatch to query both sets of logs.

Use the Amazon CloudWatch agent to send logs from the EC2 instances to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Configure AWS CloudTrail to deliver the API logs to CloudWatch Logs. Use CloudWatch Logs Insights to query both sets of logs.

Use the Amazon CloudWatch agent to send logs from the EC2 instances to Amazon Kinesis. Configure AWS CloudTrail to deliver the API logs to Kinesis. Use Kinesis to load the data into Amazon Redshift. Use Amazon Redshift to query both sets of logs.
Use the Amazon CloudWatch agent to send logs from the EC2 instances to Amazon S3. Use AWS CloudTrail to deliver the API logs to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to query both sets of logs in Amazon S3.

questions.explanation:
The Amazon CloudWatch agent can publish application logs from EC2 instances to CloudWatch Logs. AWS CloudTrail can deliver account API activity to CloudWatch Logs, and CloudWatch Logs Insights can interactively search and analyze both application and CloudTrail log groups.

**Learn more:** [Sending events to CloudWatch Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/send-cloudtrail-events-to-cloudwatch-logs.html) · [Analyzing log data with CloudWatch Logs Insights](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/AnalyzingLogData.html)
